t: Which years and engines should I buy?
x: Buy a 4.0. OffroadXtreme recommends the 1991-and-later HO, says 1987–90 Renix trucks suit owners who like diagnosing sensors, and says to avoid 1984–86 (no 4.0). NAXJA members single out non-ABS 1998–99 trucks with the 4.0, AW4, NP231 and 29-spline 8.25 as about the most solid combination. The 2000–01 trucks are good if the head has been checked or replaced.

The 2000–01 4.0 got a head with casting number 0331 that can crack between cylinders 3 and 4, letting coolant into the oil. Look through the oil filler between the cylinder 3 and 4 exhaust rockers: a 'TUPY' mark means a revised head, though Wikipedia says even those occasionally crack. Most failures follow an overheat, so keep the cooling system healthy, and never replace a cracked one with anothe

t: Which rear axle do I have, and is it any good?
x: There are three possibilities. The Dana 35 was used on early trucks and on ABS-equipped trucks throughout; it's fine stock but weak with bigger tires. The Chrysler 8.25 is common on non-ABS 1991–2001 trucks and went from 27 to 29 splines in late 1996. The Dana 44 came on some 1987–91 tow-package trucks. The axle tag or the cover shape will tell you.

From 1987 both have 2.72:1 low range. The NP231 Command-Trac is part-time (2H, 4H, N, 4L) and NAXJA calls it better for heavy off-road use. The NP242 Selec-Trac adds a full-time 4WD mode for slippery pavement.

t: What fluids and capacities does it take?
x: Per a NAXJA member's capacity summary (year not stated): 4.0 oil 6 qt with filter, coolant 10.5 qt, AW4 4 qt drain-and-fill (Dexron III/Mercon), NP231 2.2 pt, Dana 30 2.5 pt 75W-90, Dana 35 3.5 pt, 8.25 4.4 pt, plus friction modifier for Trac-Lok. ExtremeTerrain lists ATF+4 for the AW4, 12 qt of coolant, 1.6 qt for the NP231 and GL-5 oil for the AX-15, so the sources conflict: check your manual [C

The usual suspects are a clogged or cracked radiator (the factory plastic tanks can split under frame twist), a weak fan clutch, a dead electric fan or relay, an old water pump, and worn motor mounts that let the fan get too close to the radiator. On Renix trucks, check whether someone has converted the cooling system.

t: What causes death wobble, and how do I fix it?
x: Usually the track bar: worn bushings, a loose bracket or a bent bar. Worn tie-rod ends, the drag link or ball joints can also cause it. Find the loose part with a helper turning the wheel, replace it, and check the unibody around the track-bar and steering-box mounts for cracks. A new steering stabilizer only hides the problem.

NAXJA members report XJs commonly running 250,000–300,000 miles or more on factory drivetrains if they're maintained. The original poster in NAXJA's beginner thread called anything under 100,000 miles hard to find and probably overpriced.

t: Why is my Renix XJ so hard to diagnose?
x: The 1987–90 Renix computer doesn't store fault codes, so you diagnose sensors with a multimeter. It's well documented, but it's more work than the 1991-and-later Chrysler system, which became OBD-II with the JTEC computer in 1996.

t: How much lift do I need?
x: It depends on the tires and the trail. The factory Up Country package added an inch. Kits run from TeraFlex's 1.5-inch Budget Boost, through 3-inch leaf-and-coil systems from Zone and Rough Country, to 4.5–6.5-inch long-arm kits. Bigger lifts usually need an adjustable track bar and driveline work.

t: Suspension Lift — TeraFlex 1.5" Budget Boost (Quadratec), Zone Offroad 3" XJ system (Quadratec), Rough Country 3" Series II XJ kit (Quadratec), Old Man Emu (ARB)
x: The XJ responds well to a modest lift. Coils and add-a-leafs or new packs clear 30–31 in tires, and long-arm kits are for serious rock work.

t: Track Bar & Steering — JKS Manufacturing OGS126 adjustable track bar (Quadratec), Rough Country forged adjustable track bar (Quadratec), Crown RT21004 HD steering kit (Quadratec)
x: Lift moves the axle sideways and loads the steering. An adjustable track bar and heavier linkage keep it straight and wobble-free.

t: Rocker Armor — Rock Hard 4x4 RH1014 rocker sliders (Quadratec), Warrior Products under-door sideplates (Quadratec), Rock Hard 4x4
x: Unibody rockers are part of the structure. Protect them before the first rock hits.

t: Cooling — Cold Case aluminum radiator (Quadratec), CSF copper/brass radiator (Quadratec)
x: The XJ's weak spot, especially in hot climates or with a 2000–01 head you'd like to keep.

t: Axles & Lockers — Yukon Gear & Axle, ARB (Air Lockers)
x: Regearing for bigger tires and adding lockers. The 8.25 and Dana 30 are worth building, while many owners replace a Dana 35.

t: Bumpers & Recovery — Rock Hard 4x4, Rough Country
x: Stock plastic bumpers don't hold a winch or survive a stump. Steel bumpers add recovery points and approach angle.
4.0: 6.0 qt (5.7 L) with filter · 5W-30 (ExtremeTerrain) · 2.5: 4.0 qt Check the oil-filter-adapter O-rings while you're under there. They're a common leak that gets blamed on the rear main.
Panel element, 1987–2001 Crown's master filter kits (MFK8 / MFK9) bundle the oil, air and fuel filters.

Copper plugs, 0.035 in gap (4.0) · cap, rotor and wires through 1999 · coil rail on 2000–01 On 2000–01 coil-on-plug trucks, a NAXJA member notes the coil rail is expensive to replace and gets blamed for misfire codes. Rule out plugs and wiring first.

4.0: 10.5 qt (9.9 L) per the 2001 manual quote; ExtremeTerrain lists 12 qt · IAT through 2000, HOAT for 2001 (ExtremeTerrain) Flush completely when changing coolant types. On 2000–01 trucks, a healthy cooling system is your best protection against a cracked 0331 head.

Dexron III/Mercon per the NAXJA summary (ExtremeTerrain lists ATF+4; a NAXJA reply says Chrysler approved ATF+4 for the AW4 from late 2007) · 4 qt drain-and-fill, 8 qt with filter [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Do a pan drop and filter change, not a pressure flush. Check the throttle-valve cable adjustment if shifts are harsh or late.

AX-15: 3.32 qt 75W-90 GL-3/GL-4 (not GL-5) · AX-5: 3.3 qt same · NV3550: 2.1 qt Mopar 04874464AA or equivalent · ExtremeTerrain lists GL-5 for the AX-15 and AX-5 [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] NAXJA notes some owner's manuals wrongly list GL-5 for the Aisin boxes.

NP231: 2.2 pt (1.0 L) · NP242: 2.85 pt (1.3 L) · Dexron III/Mercon or ATF+3/ATF+4 · ExtremeTerrain lists 1.6 qt ATF+4 for the NP231 [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] If it pops out of 4WD or is hard to shift back to 2WD, the case may be worn.
2.5 pt (1.2 L) SAE 75W-90 Low-pinion on 2000–01 trucks, high-pinion before that. Check the inner axle seals if the knuckles are wet with gear oil.
Dana 35: 3.5 pt (1.66 L) · 8.25: 4.4 pt (2.0 L) · SAE 75W-90 (75W-140 synthetic suggested for towing) · add 4 oz friction modifier with Trac-Lok Read the tag. ABS trucks have the Dana 35.
297x/760 series (1996 and later; check earlier ABS/non-ABS sizes) Turn each front wheel to full lock and check the axle-shaft U-joints for play or rust bleeding from the caps.
Belt by year and accessory layout OffroadXtreme says to check pulley alignment: bent pulleys suggest an overtightened belt and tired bearings.
Confirm it switches on at idle Idle for 5–10 minutes and confirm the fan runs. The assemblies differ for 1987–96 and 1997–2001.
Brake fluid per the master-cylinder cap [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Larger tires may need more brake-pedal effort. Rear drums on most XJs need adjusting and fresh hardware.
Power-steering fluid [CONFIRM TYPE IN MANUAL] Check the box for seepage, and check the unibody around the box mount for cracks.

MJ Metric Ton Eliminator The Cherokee XJ turned into a compact pickup: XJ unibody up front, a fully boxed frame behind the cab, two bed lengths and the 4.0 six from 1987. 190,446 were built. A Cherokee XJ from the B-pillar forward and a fully boxed truck frame behind it. Give it the 4.0 six and a Dana 44 and it will carry a ton. About 190,000 were built, Chrysler had little reason to keep it once

t: Replace rusted floor pans and rockers
x: Wet carpet, rusty seat-bracket bolts, holes under the mats, crumbling rockers, and rust at the rear cab bulkhead where the bed meets the cab. MIG welder · cut-off wheel · spot-weld drill · clamps · weld-through primer · seam sealer · cavity wax

t: Replace a leaking clutch master cylinder
x: A soft or sinking clutch pedal, fluid on the firewall, or electrical faults from fluid dripping into the fuse box below. Comanche Club members also recommend checking the clutch-pedal welds, which some owners found incomplete and cracked. Sockets and extensions · flare-nut wrench · flashlight · brake cleaner · DOT 3 fluid

t: Hot stalls and no-starts: CPS, ballast resistor, grounds
x: The engine dies when hot and won't restart until it cools, cranks without spark, or the fuel pump won't run. Comanche Club owners name the crankshaft position sensor (CPS) and the Renix fuel-pump ballast resistor as the usual culprits, and say to check the body grounds first for strange electrical faults. Self-ranging multimeter · wire brush · dielectric grease · long extensions

Oil on the driver's side of the block and dripping off the crossmember. Comanche Club members warn that a bad adapter O-ring is often misdiagnosed as a rear main seal. Sockets · filter wrench · drain pan · degreaser · rags

t: Sort out the cooling system (and the Renix closed system)
x: Overheating on hills or in traffic, coolant loss, or a cracked pressurized plastic coolant bottle. Comanche Club members suggest replacing the plastic bottle with an aluminum one, or converting the 1987–90 Renix closed system to the later open layout. Cooling-system pressure tester · fan-clutch wrench · drain pan · funnel kit

t: Rebush the rear leaf springs and shackles
x: Clunks over bumps, a rear end that steers itself, rusted or seized shackles, or bent lower shock-mount bolts. Comanche Club owners recommend upgrading the rear lower shock mounts. Jack stands · penetrating oil · bushing press or vise · torque wrench

t: Fix or bypass the front axle disconnect (CAD)
x: 4WD that engages at the transfer case but doesn't drive the front wheels, or grinding from the front axle. Comanche Club members say to check the vacuum-operated central axle disconnect before your first trail, and to lock it in or bypass it if necessary. Vacuum gauge or hand pump · sockets · gasket scraper · RTV · gear oil

t: Cure death wobble: track bar and steering
x: Violent front shake after a bump at speed, wandering and clunks. The MJ front end is the XJ's, with the same weak points: the track bar, tie-rod ends, drag link and steering box. Helper · pry bar · tie-rod puller · torque wrench · alignment afterward

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The MJ's front end and fenders are the XJ's, so XJ consensus is a fair guide: a 235/75R15 (about 29 in) on the stock 15 in wheels fits, and a 30x9.50R15 is the practical limit, possibly rubbing the front lower control arms at full lock. NAXJA posters say a 31x10.50 needs bump stops or trimming. We found no separate MJ-only consensus. Load the bed before judging rear clearance.

t: Which years and engines should I buy?
x: Buy a 4.0. 1991–92 HO trucks have 190 hp and Chrysler's easier-to-diagnose engine management. 1987–90 Renix trucks are good too, but they're diagnosed with a multimeter. 1986 trucks have no 4.0. If you do buy a 2.5, look for 4.10 or 4.56 gears.

t: What is a Metric Ton Comanche?
x: A long-bed heavy-duty package with heavier leaf springs, wheels and tires and a Dana 44 rear axle. It raised payload from 1,400 to 2,205 lb. Sellers often don't know they have one, so check the axle and springs.

t: Which rear axle do I have?
x: The Dana 35 was standard. The Dana 44 came with the Metric Ton package (and on some other trucks; Comanche Club members' trucks include a 1992 short bed with a limited-slip Dana 44). Offroaders lists an AMC 20 as a 1986 heavy-duty option, and Quadratec's locker fitment shows the 27-spline Chrysler 8.25 on 1991–92 trucks. NAXJA: oval cover means Dana 35; angular, roughly hexagonal cover means Dana

The six-foot short bed rides on a 113 in wheelbase and arrived for 1987. The seven-foot long bed is on 119.9 in and was the only length in 1986. The short bed is better on tight trails; Metric Ton trucks are long beds. The Eliminator was short-bed only, per Comanche Club.
Under the carpet, at the rear cab bulkhead and window seals, where the bed meets the cab, and where the unibody meets the rear frame. NAXJA members say bulging rail bottoms mean rust inside.

Drivetrain and front-end parts are shared with the XJ and easy to find. Comanche Club members say everything behind the doors is different, and the bed, tailgate, taillights and bench-seat sliders are MJ-specific and scarce. An XJ fuel pump and sender don't fit without fabrication.

t: How much can it tow and carry?
x: Kelley Blue Book lists a 1992 Comanche at 5,000 lb maximum towing and 1,475 lb payload. Wikipedia gives 1,400 lb for a standard truck and 2,205 lb for the Metric Ton package.
From 1987 the NP231 Command-Trac is part-time and the NP242 Selec-Trac adds a full-time 4WD mode. Both have 2.72:1 low range. 1986 trucks used the NP207 and NP228, both with 2.61:1 low range.

t: Why does my MJ stall when hot?
x: Usually the crankshaft position sensor, which can fail when hot and test fine cold, or, on Renix trucks, the fuel-pump ballast resistor. Comanche Club members say to check the body grounds first for any strange electrical fault.
AMC and Chrysler built 190,446. Comanche Club members got 2021 vehicle-in-operation figures from Key Parts showing about 18,600 registered in the US and Canada.

t: Suspension Lift — Rough Country 3 in lift kit, Comanche MJ (Quadratec), Rough Country 4.5 in lift kit, Comanche MJ (Quadratec), Rough Country 6.5 in X-Series lift kit, Comanche MJ (Quadratec)
x: MJ-specific kits handle the longer rear springs. A modest lift clears 31s and keeps the truck useful.

t: Shackles & Driveline — Rough Country adjustable lift shackles, XJ/MJ (Quadratec), Rough Country transfer case lowering kit, XJ/MJ (Quadratec), Crown RT21045 HD greasable shackle kit (Quadratec)
x: Lift shackles level the rear. A transfer-case drop corrects driveline angles after a lift.

t: Steering — Rough Country heavy-duty tie rod, XJ/MJ (Quadratec), Rough Country drop pitman arm, XJ/MJ (Quadratec), Rancho RS62109 adjustable track bar (Quadratec)
x: Bigger tires and lifts load the XJ-style steering. Heavier tie rods and a drop pitman arm keep it straight.

t: Axles & Lockers — USA Standard Spartan locker, Chrysler 8.25 (Quadratec), Yukon Gear & Axle, ARB (Air Lockers)
x: Owners commonly replace a Dana 35 or build a Dana 44 or 8.25. Comanche Club members say proper gearing makes a 4.0 feel like a V8.

t: Rust Repair Panels — Key Parts rocker panel, Comanche MJ (Quadratec), Key Parts rear fender panel, Comanche MJ (Quadratec), Key Parts front lower quarter section, MJ 7 ft bed (Quadratec)
x: Rockers, inner rockers and bed panels are what keep MJs on the road.

t: Lighting — Oracle LED tail lights, Comanche MJ (Quadratec), Crown RT28005 H4 headlight conversion (Quadratec)
x: Original sealed beams and tired taillight grounds are a safety issue. Since MJ taillights are hard to find, new ones are worth buying.
4.0: 6.0 qt (5.7 L) with filter · 2.5: 4.0 qt (XJ figures) Renix-era engines use a metric filter thread. Comanche Club members advise against Fram filters.

t: Ignition: plugs, wires, cap and rotor
x: Copper plugs, 0.035 in gap (4.0, XJ figure) Clean the throttle body and IAC and set the TPS to spec while you're there; Comanche Club calls this routine on an old MJ.
4.0: about 10.5 qt (XJ figure) [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Check the plastic bottle for cracks. Renix trucks have the pressurized closed system.
DOT 3 brake fluid Look for leaks above the fuse box.
4 qt drain-and-fill, 8 qt with filter (XJ figure) · Dexron III/Mercon per the 2001 manual quote [CONFIRM FOR YOUR YEAR] Do a pan drop and filter change, not a pressure flush.
AX-15 and AX-5: about 3.3 qt 75W-90 GL-3/GL-4, not GL-5 (NAXJA) · BA-10/5: [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] NAXJA notes some manuals wrongly list GL-5 for the Aisin boxes.
NP231: 2.2 pt · NP242: 2.85 pt · ATF (XJ figures) 1986 trucks have the NP207 or NP228; check the tag.
2.5 pt (1.2 L) SAE 75W-90 (XJ figure) Check that the vacuum axle disconnect actually engages before the first trail.

Dana 35: 3.5 pt · 8.25: 4.4 pt (XJ figures) · Dana 44: [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · SAE 75W-90 · friction modifier with Trac-Lok Read the axle tag first. Comanche Club members note that some Dana 35s have a metal fill plug, not the rubber one most people expect.
Front axle shafts and both driveshafts Turn the front wheels to full lock and check the axle U-joints for play.
DOT 3 fluid · front discs, rear drums Rear drums usually need adjusting and fresh hardware. Comanche Club has a brake-upgrade write-up.

Engine, body, taillight and fuel-tank grounds Comanche Club members recommend a headlight relay harness for brighter lights and less load on the switch. If you remove the bed, re-ground the harness or it won't start.

YJ The first Wrangler, with square headlights and leaf springs. Track bars and anti-roll bars made it more civil than the CJ. The Wrangler that dared to have square headlights, and spent thirty years being forgiven for it. Under the controversial face it's a wider, calmer CJ-7 on leaf springs, and from 1991 it has the 4.0 straight-six. Buy that one, check the frame, and enjoy the cheapest ticket t

t: Fix the vacuum front-axle disconnect (or convert to cable)
x: 4WD light stays off, the front axle won't drive in 4H, or it engages and drops out with a clunk under load at speed. Hand vacuum pump with gauge · vacuum hose and connectors · check valve · gasket for the disconnect cover.

t: Replace the clutch and internal slave cylinder (early YJs)
x: Sinking or spongy clutch pedal, fluid loss from the clutch reservoir, a slipping clutch after fluid has soaked the disc, and fluid at the bottom of the bellhousing. Transmission jack · flare-nut wrenches · clutch alignment tool · torque wrench · brake washer (treat old linings as if they contain asbestos) · DOT 3/4 fluid.

t: Rebuild the 4.2's Carter BBD feedback carburetor (1987–90)
x: Stalling, flooding, hunting idle, loss of power or running hot. Many of these are vacuum leaks or ignition faults rather than the carburetor itself. T-gauge · hand vacuum pump · timing light · carb cleaner · alcohol · thread locker · Mopar or Echlin/NAPA premium rebuild kit (Ludel's preference).

t: Replace leaf springs, shackles and bushings
x: Sagging or uneven ride height, clunks over bumps, cracked or squeezed-out bushings, broken leaves and rusted shackles. Jack stands · floor jack · press or vise for bushings · wire brush · grease · torque wrench · new U-bolts.

t: Replace the rear main seal (4.0 / 4.2 six)
x: Oil dripping from where the engine meets the bellhousing, and an oily transmission and crossmember. Rule out the valve cover and oil pan gaskets first, because oil runs downhill. Pick · thin punch · torque wrench · RTV · oil pan gasket · new oil and filter.

t: Cut out and replace rusted floor pans
x: Soft, flaking or holed metal under the driver's carpet, water in the footwell, and rust around the seat and roll-bar mounts. Cut-off wheel · grinder · MIG welder · clamps · seam sealer · primer and paint.

t: Chase down front-end shimmy and worn steering
x: A violent side-to-side shake after a bump at around 45 mph, wandering, or a clunk when you turn the wheel with the engine off. Pry bar · floor jack and stands · torque wrench · helper.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: A stock YJ usually takes 30-inch tires on stock rims without trouble. Four Wheel Trends says 31x10.50s can be squeezed on, but they may need wheels with different backspacing and can still rub, so don't wheel that setup hard without a lift.

Most buyers want a 1991–1995 truck with the fuel-injected 4.0 six. Hagerty calls it often the most desirable engine and says it commands a larger premium over the four. For 1987–90, Hagerty says the four- and six-cylinder versions differ by only a few hundred dollars in #3 condition.

t: Why does the YJ have square headlights?
x: Neither Wikipedia nor Hagerty gives an official reason. Wikipedia says only that the rectangular lamps set it apart from the round-eyed CJs. The TJ brought round headlights back for 1997. Owners who can't live with them fit round-headlight conversion kits.

t: My 4WD light won't come on. Is the transfer case broken?
x: Probably not. The YJ front axle is engaged by a vacuum motor, and Quadratec says dry-rotted, cracked or disconnected vacuum lines are the usual culprit. Test the system with a hand vacuum pump before buying parts, or convert to a cable-operated disconnect.

t: Should I avoid the Peugeot gearbox?
x: Six-cylinder YJs from 1987–89 could have the Peugeot BA-10/5 five-speed, which ExtremeTerrain describes as historically unreliable. Wikipedia lists the Aisin AX-15 behind the 4.2 from 1989, and the AX-15 stayed with the 4.0 through 1995. Four-cylinder trucks use the AX-5.
The NP207 was used on 1987 YJs only, and ExtremeTerrain calls it a poor unit. The NP231, used from 1988 onward, is the stronger and far better-supported case. A 1988–95 YJ will have the NP231.

t: Which years have the internal clutch slave cylinder?
x: Sources disagree. 4WD Mechanix says 1987–92 YJs used a slave cylinder built into the release bearing and that 1993 brought the external slave and pivot arm used in the TJ. Wikipedia dates the move outside the bellhousing to 1994, and Advance Adapters lists its internal-bearing hose kit for 1987–93. Treat 1993 as either, and look for an external slave on the bellhousing. The internal type means pul

t: What fluids do the axles and transfer case take?
x: Quadratec's factory-based chart lists GL-5 80W-90 or 75W-140 synthetic for the Dana 30, Dana 35 and Dana 44, with 4 oz of limited-slip additive for a Trac-Lok. ExtremeTerrain recommends 75W-140 in the rear for warm-weather towing. The NP231 takes automatic transmission fluid (ExtremeTerrain lists ATF+3 or ATF+4); Quadratec's chart gives 2.2 pints for the NP231 and 4.4 pints for the NP207. Haynes'

t: Can the 4.2's carburetor be made reliable?
x: Yes. Moses Ludel's 4WD Mechanix guide says the Carter BBD can be reliable when rebuilt to factory specs, and that a clogged fuel filter, a weak mechanical pump or a vacuum leak can mimic carburetor faults. He calls Mopar's multi-point injection conversion the bigger upgrade.

t: Is a YJ a good investment?
x: Hagerty puts a median #3-condition YJ at about $8,100, against $9,900 for an earlier CJ-7. Its Hagerty Vehicle Rating is 86 and climbing while the CJ's has fallen, although Hagerty says the rating is not a predictor of future collectability. Renegades bring the most, followed by Saharas and Islanders.

t: What's the difference between the Sahara, Islander and Renegade?
x: The Sahara (from 1988) included most options, with body-color flares, green trail-cloth seats and fog lamps. The Islander (1988–93) had sunset graphics and body-color flares and steps. The Renegade Decor Group (October 1990–94) added the 4.0, 8-inch alloy wheels and a widebody look.

t: Springs & Suspension — Old Man Emu (ARB), Quadratec — YJ lift kits & suspension, Warrior Products
x: Fresh leaf packs and urethane bushings transform a tired YJ, and a mild lift clears 31s. Spring-over-axle conversions are the classic path to bigger tires.

t: Axle Disconnect & Steering — JKS Posi-Lok PSL900 (ExtremeTerrain), Quadratec — YJ steering & brakes
x: A cable-operated front-axle disconnect removes the vacuum system that strands so many YJs in 2WD.

t: Gears & Lockers — Yukon Gear & Axle, ARB USA (Air Lockers), Quadratec — YJ driveline
x: Bigger tires need lower gears, and a locker turns the YJ's short wheelbase into a proper crawler.

t: Transmission & Engine Swaps — Advance Adapters, Novak Conversions
x: Replacing a Peugeot BA-10 or dropping a 4.0 into a four-cylinder truck is well-trodden ground, with adapters and mounts off the shelf.

t: Bumpers & Winches — Warn, Quadratec — YJ bumpers, Rugged Ridge
x: The factory bumpers are thin. A steel bumper with a winch mount is the first piece of armor most YJs get.

t: Armor & Skids — Quadratec — YJ armor & protection
x: Rocker guards and skid plates protect the tub and the low-slung transfer case.

t: Tops & Doors — Quadratec — YJ soft tops
x: Half doors, a fresh soft top or a hardtop: the YJ is still a convertible at heart.

SAE 10W-30 (Quadratec); ExtremeTerrain lists 10W-30 or 5W-30 · ≈4 qt (2.5) / 6 qt (4.0, 4.2) with filter (Quadratec) Drain-plug torque: ExtremeTerrain's TJ-era table gives 25 ft-lb for the 2.5 and 4.0 [CONFIRM IN MANUAL for your YJ]. Carter BBD feedback carburetor · mechanical fuel pump Ludel says a clogged filter, a weak mechanical pump or a vacuum leak can mimic carburetor faults. Replace brittle vacuum hose before rebuilding anything.

Check the Dana 30 disconnect housing and pinion seals for leaks.
Shift motor, check valve, reserve tank and hoses Quadratec lists dry-rotted or cracked vacuum lines as the usual cause of a YJ that won't engage 4WD.

Now it's one of the cheapest ways into coil springs, solid axles and a 4.0 or Magnum
