t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: Factory sizes were 205R16 and 235/70R16, which are almost the same height. On a stock-height, stock-geared truck, a LandyZone owner recommends going no bigger than 245/75R16 (about 30.5 inches), which several members run. Owners do run 33s and bigger with lifts; one member says 35s want at least a 4.1 and ideally a 4.37 ring and pinion.

t: When was it sold in the US?
x: From the 1994 to 1998 model years, always with the V8: 3.9 litres with Lucas 14CUX injection at first, then the GEMS-managed '4.0' (same 3,946 cc) from 1996 for OBD-II.

t: How is it related to the Range Rover Classic and Defender?
x: It uses the Range Rover Classic's chassis, suspension and four-wheel-drive system, much of its body structure, and the same LT230 transfer box and Tdi engines as the Defender of the same era.

t: Can I import a diesel Disco 1 into the US?
x: Every Discovery Series I was built by 1998, so all of them are now more than 25 years old. NHTSA allows vehicles at least 25 years old (from date of manufacture) to be imported without meeting FMVSS; check EPA and your state's rules and make sure the VIN and build date line up.

The 300Tdi is the enthusiast favourite: mechanical, economical and shared with the Defender, though it needs the revised timing kit. The 200Tdi is cruder but similar. The V8 is smoother and easy to source in the US but thirsty and sensitive to cooling problems.

t: What fuel economy should I expect from the V8?
x: Not much. One owner of a 3.9 V8 reported about 10.5 mpg (imperial) at 100–120 km/h and was trying to get closer to 14. Tired V8s lose economy as the camshaft wears, according to experienced members.

Two inches is the common, sensible lift using longer springs and extended shocks; owners advise lowering the bump stops so the body isn't damaged at full compression. Owners running bigger lifts fit caster-corrected (6-degree) arms and wide-angle propshafts, and regear for big tyres.
Yes, badly. The usual places are the sills, rear floor and boot floor, inner wings, body mounts and the rear chassis around the crossmember. Three-doors are reported to be worse.

The plastic surround leaks where it meets the metal roof, the frame seal is flimsy, and the drain tubes and cups split with age. LandyZone owners call the drain installation 'appalling'. Resealing and new drains usually cure it.

t: Which Discoveries did the Camel Trophy use?
x: The Discovery was the main Camel Trophy vehicle from 1990 to 1997: 200Tdis from Siberia (1990, three-door) to South America (1994), then 300Tdis from 1995 to Mongolia in 1997. Japan and Germany also got Sandglow Camel Trophy special editions.
A badge-engineered Discovery 1 sold in Japan by Honda, a product of Rover's cross-holding with Honda that ended when BMW bought Rover in 1994.

t: Suspension Lift — Old Man Emu (ARB), Terrafirma
x: Springs sag after 25-plus years. Longer springs and shocks restore height and add room for 245/75s or 33s.
An ATB centre differential in the LT230 removes much of the driveline backlash; uprated shafts and lockers suit bigger tyres.

x: Sills, floors and body mounts are the Disco 1's weak point; repair panels are the difference between a project and a scrapper.

x: When the frame is thin everywhere, a galvanised replacement is the permanent fix; LandyZone members have priced Maer's 300Tdi frame.

x: ABS, TC and HDC warning lights on together, sometimes intermittently. Diagnostic tool, multimeter, big torque wrench for hubs · wheel-speed sensors, hub assembly

Flaking or holed metal at the rear crossmember, rear chassis legs and around the fuel tank; collapsed suspension hangers; MOT failures. MIG welder, grinder, axle stands, tank support · rear quarter or half chassis, crossmember, body mounts

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: Discoweb owners recommend 245/75R16 for a stock-height truck. Several run 265/75R16 at stock height, but they rub at full lock on the plastic behind the fog lamps or need the front bumper trimmed. With a 2-inch lift such as the OME kit, 265/75R16 is the common choice; 285/75R16 wants nearer 3 inches and raises gearing and halfshaft-strength concerns.

The Td5 makes its torque low down and responds well to tuning, but it needs a diagnostic tool for some jobs and has known weak spots: the injector harness, the fuel pressure regulator, the early oil-pump bolt and, increasingly, cylinder heads. The V8 is smoother and quicker than a stock Td5 but thirsty, and head gaskets and liners are its big risks. In the US every Disco 2 is a V8.

Pocketed headlamps, revised rear lamps with the indicators moved up out of the bumper, the centre diff lock lever back as an option (standard on high-spec trucks) and, in North America, the 4.6 V8 instead of the 4.0. Td5s had already gained Euro 3 tune and EGR in 2002.

t: Does my truck have a centre diff lock?
x: Every Series II has a lockable centre differential in the LT230, but early trucks were built without the lever. Owners fit a Discovery 1 linkage from a truck with the same transmission (manual and auto parts differ) or a kit such as Ashcroft's. On early trucks, don't cut the CDL input wire to the ABS ECU: the ECU uses it to stop traction control fighting the locked diff.

Opinion is split. ACE fans say the truck corners far better and has more articulation off-road; others fit standard anti-roll bars once the pipes or valve block start leaking. Repairs to a tired system can run to thousands, so price it before you buy.

t: Can I convert the SLS to coils?
x: Yes, and it's a common job. Fit Discovery 2 rear spring seats (Discovery 1 seats are shallower), coils and matching shocks, or a ready kit from Terrafirma, Rovers North or Atlantic British. The SLS then needs switching off with dealer software or an aftermarket tool.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: The EPA rated a 2002 4.0 V8 automatic at 12 mpg city, 16 highway and 13 combined, and a 2003 4.6 at 11 city, 14 highway and 12 combined. Td5s do much better, though no US figure exists because they were never sold there.
Australian specs for a 2001 Td5 manual list 3,500 kg (7,716 lb) braked and 750 kg unbraked, with a 2,750 kg gross vehicle mass.

t: Can I import a Td5 Discovery 2 into the US?
x: Once it is 25 years old by date of manufacture, yes: NHTSA exempts it from FMVSS. Series IIs were built from 1998 to May 2004, so as of October 2026 trucks built before October 2001 qualify, and later Td5s follow month by month. Check EPA and state rules as well.

t: What fluids does the Td5 take?
x: discovery2.co.uk's owner uses 5W-30 fully synthetic, the same oil his dealer used, with 7.2 litres including both filters. The transfer box and both axles take 75W-90 gear oil: about 2.0 litres to refill the LT230 (2.3 from dry) and about 3.5 litres for the two axles together.

t: How is it related to the Discovery 1 and the P38?
x: It keeps the Discovery 1's 100-inch ladder frame and LT230, but borrows a lot from the P38: the 4.0 'Thor' V8, the 5x120 wheel pattern and the front ball joints. The rear propshaft coupling fits Discovery 1, Discovery 2 and P38.

t: Suspension Lift — Old Man Emu 2" kit (Lucky8), Terrafirma TFXT Plus 3" kit (Lucky8)
x: Two inches with stiffer springs and longer shocks clears 265/75s and restores sagging trucks; 3-inch kits need more work on props and geometry.

t: Air-To-Coil Conversion — Terrafirma TF226 (LR Direct), Rovers North RNK5118 rear kit
x: Replaces leaking SLS air springs and a tired compressor with coils, at stock height or lifted.

t: Centre Diff Lock — Ashcroft Transmissions — Disco II difflock
x: Early trucks have the lock but no lever; a linkage kit gives you a proper locked centre diff for mud and steep climbs.
Sills are low and soft; sliders protect them and the body behind.

t: Propshafts — Tom Wood's D2 rear double-cardan shaft (Lucky8)
x: Lifted trucks need more angle than the stock rubber coupler and non-greasable double-cardan joint like to give.

x: Rear chassis sections, crossmembers, sills and body mounts are what keep a Disco 2 on the road.

t: Rebuild or replace the air suspension compressor

Uneven ride height, suspension warning lights, or a truck that won't hold the height it's asked for. Height-sensor faults are one of the electrical causes of air-suspension trouble. Basic sockets, dielectric grease, diagnostic tool for calibration · LR020155 (FL) / LR020157 (FR) / LR020159 (RL) / LR020161 (RR)

The parking brake won't apply or release, or the motor grinds or whines without effect. A seized EPB can leave the truck stuck. Torx bits, sockets, patience · gear repair kit DA9223 · actuator LR019223 · parking brake shoes LR031947

t: Front lower control arms and bushes
x: Clunks, vague steering, tyre wear, split boots and oil leaking from the hydraulic rear bush. Torque wrench to about 300 Nm, 18/21/22 mm sockets, reciprocating saw with carbide blades, heat, 3-jaw puller · arm kit with hardware · bush LR073366

Judder, flare or harsh shifts, an unknown service history, or a weeping valve body sleeve. Sockets, fluid pump, scan tool or thermometer for the level check · pan LR007474 · sleeve TZV500010 · ATF TYK500050

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: On 18-inch wheels, 265/65R18 or 285/60R18 (about 31 in) fit at factory height without modification. 275/65R18 (about 32 in) is about the biggest that works at stock height, and owners report it needs the front-left height-sensor wire zip-tied to the frame rail and a little liner reshaping; one owner's 285/65R18s rubbed slightly at full lock. With lift rods, 275/65R18 is the common choice. One owne

Sort of. Land Rover's Integrated Body Frame builds the engine bay and cabin as a monocoque, then joins them to a basic ladder frame that carries the gearbox and suspension. It is heavier than a pure monocoque but stronger and tougher.

In the US the choice is the 300 hp 4.4 V8 (all years) or the 216 hp 4.0 V6 (2005–07). The V8 is the common one, shared with the 2006–09 Range Rover Sport and L322 Range Rover. Elsewhere most trucks have the 195 hp, 440 Nm 2.7 TDV6, which is far more economical but carries crank-bearing and timing-belt risks.

t: Is the TDV6 crank failure real?
x: Yes, though it's uncommon. Land Rover bulletin SSM71816 covers crankshaft and main-bearing failures, mainly caused by incorrectly located bearing shells at assembly. Symptoms are a knock or rumble that worsens under load, sometimes with the oil-pressure light. Carbuyer calls it rare, unpredictable and very costly.
7,716 lb (3,500 kg) braked and 1,654 lb (750 kg) unbraked, according to Land Rover's launch specifications.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: EPA ratings for the V8 are 12–13 mpg city and 17 highway, depending on year; the V6 is rated 13/18 for 2005. In the UK, PistonHeads quotes 27.2 mpg (imperial) for the automatic TDV6 and 18.8 mpg for the V8.

The cheap route is lift rods, which replace the links on the factory height sensors so the air suspension sits about 2–2.5 in higher (Proud Rhino, Terrafirma and Lucky8 make them). A diagnostic tool such as Gap's IIDTool can change the programmed heights instead. If you've had enough of air, Terrafirma sells +2 in coil conversions and Old Man Emu coil springs for the LR3 are sold too.

Every truck has a computer-controlled, progressively locking centre differential. A locking rear differential (Land Rover's electronic torque managed unit) was optional. Terrain Response controls how hard both lock in each mode.

t: What goes wrong with the air suspension?
x: Leaking air springs, height sensors, compressors and the electrics. A failing compressor overheats and slows; if ignored, the dryer desiccant can break down and damage the valve blocks. Many owners rebuild the Hitachi compressor; the later AMK unit needs a software update to fit.

t: My parking brake is stuck. How do I release it?
x: PistonHeads says a seized EPB can be released manually using the jack handle through a metal loop behind a plastic panel. The underlying fault is usually the actuator or its cable adjustment, and dirt build-up is a known cause.

t: What's the difference between an LR3 and a Discovery 3?
x: Nothing structural: LR3 is the North American and Middle Eastern name. The engines differ by market, with the V8 and V6 petrols in North America and the TDV6 diesel as the main engine elsewhere.
Land Rover's launch specification quotes a 700 mm (27.6 in) wading depth. Raise the suspension to off-road height before you go in.

t: Lift Rods & Height Tuning — Proud Rhino PR25 lift rods (via Lucky8), Terrafirma +2 in lift rod kit (via Lucky8), Gap Diagnostic — IIDTool
x: Longer height-sensor links trick the air suspension into running about 2–2.5 in higher with no electronics. A diagnostic tool can do the same in software and calibrate the sensors after repairs.

x: For owners who want to stop chasing air leaks: coil springs and dampers replace the air struts, with a module to keep the warning lights off.

t: Rock Sliders — Lucky8 CFE rock sliders, Proud Rhino rock sliders (via Lucky8), Terrafirma LR3/LR4 rock sliders (via Lucky8)
x: The sills are low and expensive to fix. Bolt-on sliders protect them on rocks and ruts.

x: Skid plates for the sump, gearbox and fuel tank, because the independent suspension leaves more of the underside exposed than a beam-axle truck.

x: Polyurethane bushes outlast the factory rubber on a heavy truck, especially in the front lower arms.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: US trucks came on 255/50R19 or 255/50R20. On the 20s, LandRoverWorld owners say 265/50R20 fits at standard height without rubbing and is the largest size that still fits the spare well when fully inflated. A 285/50R20 rubs slightly at full lock and needs the spare deflated to fit underneath. Owners who switch to aftermarket 18-inch wheels run 265/65R18 with no rubbing at standard height; 285/60R18

The 2010–2013 V8 makes 375 hp and 375 lb-ft and has a two-speed transfer box as standard, but 2010–2012 engines in the bulletin's VIN range can need timing-chain tensioners. The 2014–2016 V6 makes 340 hp and 332 lb-ft, gets the eight-speed and a better EPA rating (16 vs 14 mpg combined), but has its own supercharger-isolator and cooling-pipe issues, and needs the HD package for low range.

t: Does my LR4 have low range and a rear locker?
x: All 2010–2013 US LR4s have the two-speed transfer box. Owners disagree on whether every 2010–2013 truck also got the rear locker, so check physically or with a VIN decode. For 2014–2016, low range and the active rear locker came only with the Heavy Duty package ($1,350), which also included a full-size spare.

t: Is the 5.0 timing-chain problem a deal-breaker?
x: No, if it's been done or priced in. Bulletin LTB00474 covers 2010–2012 LR4s in VIN range AA513326–CA652214, and the fix is new tensioners and steel-insert levers (8.1 hours of labour by Land Rover's own timing). Owners believe later 2012 and 2013 engines got the updated parts from the factory, and many stress shorter oil-change intervals.

t: How often should I replace the coolant crossover pipes?
x: There's no factory interval, but owners treat them as a maintenance item: failures are reported from about 50,000 miles, replacement every 60,000 is considered cautious, and past 100,000 miles original pipes are 'borrowed time'. The SC V6 can overheat quickly once coolant is lost, so don't ignore a coolant smell.

t: What oil does it take, and how much?
x: The 5.0 V8 takes SAE 5W-20 meeting WSS-M2C925-A, about 8.0 litres (17 US pints) with the filter. Land Rover's 2014 service bulletin also specifies 5W-20 to WSS-M2C925-A for the SC V6, and owners say 2015–16 handbooks call for 0W-20 to STJLR.51.5122. The oil level is shown electronically rather than on a conventional dipstick, and most owners extract the old oil from the top and change the cartridg

The advertised maximum is 7,716 lb (3,500 kg) braked, and the gross train weight is 14,859 lb. One LandRoverWorld owner tows a 6,600-lb boat and trailer and came away impressed. The Discovery 4 also added Trailer Stability Assist.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: EPA ratings: 12/17 mpg city/highway (14 combined) for the 2010 V8, 13/17 for 2013, and 15/19 (16 combined) for the 2014–2016 SC V6, all on premium. An Expedition Portal V8 owner averages about 14 mpg. The petrol tank holds 86 litres (23 US gal).

t: Can I lift it and keep the air suspension?
x: Yes. Lift rods that replace the height-sensor links, such as Proud Rhino's PR25, raise it about 2.5 in with no reprogramming. One LandRoverWorld owner found that strut spacers with 18-inch wheels drove far better than lift rods with wheel spacers. If you're done with air altogether, Terrafirma sells a +2 in air-to-coil conversion.

t: Which scan tool do owners use?
x: The GAP IIDTool is the common choice. Owners use it to reset ride height and to match the EAS software to a replacement Hitachi or AMK compressor. A generic OBD-II reader can't do those jobs.
Land Rover quotes 700 mm (28 in) at off-road height and 600 mm (24 in) at standard height.

t: Was the diesel sold in the US?
x: No. US LR4s were petrol-only: the 5.0 V8 for 2010–2013 and the 3.0 SC V6 for 2014–2016. The TDV6 and SDV6 diesels were sold elsewhere.

t: Suspension Lift — Proud Rhino PR25 lift rods (via Lucky8), Lucky8 CFELK2.5 lift rod kit, Terrafirma +2 in air-to-coil kit TF266 (via Lucky8)
x: Longer height-sensor links trick the air suspension into riding about 2.5 in higher with no programming. Coil conversions trade air's adjustability for simplicity.

t: Underbody Armor & Sliders — Proud Rhino bash plate system, Proud Rhino rock sliders, Lucky8 CFE rock sliders
x: The LR4's low-slung sills, fuel tank and air compressor are exposed on rocks. Frame-mounted sliders and aluminium bash plates fix that.

t: Winch Bumper — Proud Rhino LR4 heavy-duty front winch bumper
x: A steel front bumper adds a winch mount and recovery points while keeping the approach angle usable.

t: Roof Racks — Front Runner Slimline II LR3/LR4 kit (via Lucky8), Terrafirma TF972 roof rack (via Lucky8)
x: The LR4's long, flat roof is made for a full-length rack; Land Rover rates it for 75 kg (165 lb) including the rack.

t: Cooling Upgrades — Lucky8 5.0 V8 upgraded cooling kit, Lucky8 3.0 SC V6 upgraded cooling kit
x: Aluminium replacements for the plastic crossover pipes and manifolds are the most popular reliability mod on both engines.
Air-suspension calibration and matching the software to a replacement compressor need more than an OBD-II reader.
Dropping from 19s or 20s to 18s buys sidewall for airing down and far more all-terrain and mud-terrain tyre choices.

Lexus got into the off-road business the way a rich kid gets into punk rock: by borrowing a band that was already good. The first LX 450, which reached US buyers as a 1996 model, was almost entirely the J80 Land Cruiser with leather, wood and a new grille. Every LX since has been built on the Land Cruiser of its day, from the 100 Series-based LX 470 through the 200 Series-based LX 570 to today's 3

J80 FZJ80 1FZ-FE The first Lexus truck, a lightly disguised 80 Series Land Cruiser with a 212-hp 4.5-liter straight-six. Sold for two US model years only. An 80 Series Land Cruiser that went to the tailor and came back with cladding, softer springs and a $7,000 premium. Under the leather it still has solid axles at both ends, which is exactly why people want one.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The stock size is 275/70R16. On a stock-height 80 Series or LX 450 with healthy springs, the usual answer is 285/75R16, about 33 in. Owners report it works, with some rubbing possible at full flex or full lock. Anything bigger starts rubbing. Slee's guide notes that 35s are possible with a 2-in Old Man Emu lift, but expect to rub when crawling unless you lower the bump stops.

A 1997 spec sheet lists a 2,268 kg (5,000 lb) maximum trailer weight. Slee warns that the four bolt holes in the black rear crossmember (covered by trim on the LX) aren't rated for towing in the US, so use a frame-mounted receiver hitch.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: The EPA rates both years at 12 mpg city, 14 highway and 13 combined on regular fuel. Bigger tires and a roof rack push that lower.

t: What fluids and capacities does it take?
x: According to AMSOIL's 1997 LX 450 lookup: engine oil 7.8 qt with filter (10W-30 above -18°C, 5W-30 below 10°C). Coolant 14.8 qt with the front heater only, or 15.9 qt with front and rear heaters. The A343F transmission takes 11.6 qt total. The transfer case takes 3.6 pt of GL-4 or GL-5 gear oil. The front diff takes 5.5 pt (with locker) or 5.9 pt (without) and the rear diff 7 pt, both GL-5 90-weig

Every LX 450 has a center differential that locks automatically in low range. Electric front and rear axle lockers were a factory option, and BaT listings describe triple-locked trucks. If yours has them there are locker controls on the dash. Test them in low range on a loose surface before you buy. For unlocked trucks Slee recommends ARB Air Lockers, which cost less than retrofitting the factory

t: Can I lock the center diff in high range?
x: Not from the factory. US trucks from 1993 on had the switch deleted but kept the wiring. A plug-in CDL switch (Slee TOY1002 for 1995–1997) adds high-range locking in under an hour.

t: How worried should I be about the head gasket?
x: Worried enough to budget for it, but not enough to panic. Expedition Portal regulars say 1995–1997 1FZ-FEs are the ones to watch, and that risk climbs past 150k and especially 200k miles, with overheating in hot climates as a trigger. A properly done gasket job with receipts adds about $1,500–$2,000 in value. Others note plenty of unreplaced gaskets go past 200k without trouble.

t: Should I regear for bigger tires?
x: The 1FZ-FE trucks come with 4.11 gears. Slee suggests regearing to 4.56, 4.88 or 5.29 when you go up in tire size. Opinions vary on the right ratio, so its advice is to drive a truck with the setup you're considering first.

t: What's the difference between an LX 450 and a 1996–1997 Land Cruiser?
x: Mechanically, very little. The LX has softer suspension, extra sound deadening, softer leather, auto climate control, a console subwoofer, body cladding, larger rear bumper corners and two-tone mud flaps. The LX mud flaps don't swap onto a Toyota. Parts and aftermarket kits for the FZJ80 fit both.

Old Man Emu coil-and-shock kits are the classic answer. Slee's guide mentions OME 2-in lifts with 35s, and owners run OME 850/864-series coils. Metal Tech 4x4 sells 1.5-in and 2-in front spacer plates, adjustable rear upper and offset lower links, sway-bar drop brackets and caster plates for the 80 Series and LX 450. If you lift the truck, readjust the load-sensing brake proportioning valve.

There are only two, and they're nearly the same. The 1996 and 1997 trucks both have the A343F, airbags and OBD-II. Buy the one with the best records, the healthiest knuckles and working lockers. Factory lockers add about $2,500 in value according to forum regulars, so a locked truck is worth the wait.

t: Suspension Lift — Old Man Emu, Metal Tech 4x4 (spacers, links, caster plates)
x: A mild lift with better shocks gets you on 33s without rubbing. Adjustable rear links and caster plates keep the geometry right as you go taller.
If the truck didn't come with factory lockers, air lockers are cheaper than retrofitting the electric ones, and the OEM switch and dash lights can be wired to run them.

t: Rock Sliders — Metal Tech 4x4 (80 Series / LX 450 sliders), Slee Off-Road
x: The cladding and running boards are fragile and the rocker panels are expensive. Frame-mounted sliders protect both and still work as a step.

t: Bumpers & Swing-Outs — Dissent Off-Road (LC80), Slee Off-Road
x: A real front bumper carries a winch and protects the radiator. A rear bumper with a swing-out carrier lifts a full-size spare off the ground.
The stock air intake is in the passenger front fender. A snorkel moves it to roof height for water crossings. Slee says to fit one for wading, not for the debated performance gains.

t: Maintenance Parts — Cruiser Corps (80 Series), CruiserTeq (80 Series & LX 450)
x: At this age the knuckles, hoses and seals matter more than the accessories. Specialist shops stock kits by chassis.
10W-30 (above −18°C) or 5W-30 (below 10°C) · 7.8 qt with filter Drain plug torque is 18 ft-lb. An oil analysis on the first drain gives a useful head-gasket baseline. Look for coolant in the oil.
1FZ-FE panel element Check the intake hose and boot for cracks. IH8MUD regulars list a worn intake hose as a common 80 Series fault.

Denso OEM plugs [CONFIRM GAP IN MANUAL] The 1FZ-FE uses a distributor and plug wires, so replace the wires with the plugs on an unknown truck. Spark plug tube seals stop oil pooling in the plug wells.

Toyota red coolant · 14.8 qt (front heater) / 15.9 qt (front + rear heaters) Overheating is what kills 1FZ head gaskets. Expedition Portal regulars say to use Toyota red only and to check the water pump, fan clutch and thermostat. A replaced radiator or crud in the overflow bottle are clues to past overheating (Slee).
Rubber hoses under the intake, driver's side The PHH and the bypass hoses above it can strand you when they fail. Original clamps mean original hoses.

Dexron III-type ATF (AMSOIL lists AF3 for the A343F) · 11.6 qt total fill A pan drain only replaces part of the 11.6 qt, so repeat the drain-and-fill a couple of times rather than pressure-flushing an old transmission.
GL-4 or GL-5 gear oil · 3.6 pt The center diff is viscous-coupled on these trucks. Note any binding or clunks in tight turns on pavement.

GL-5 90 (80W-90 below −18°C) · front 5.5 pt with locker / 5.9 pt without · rear 7 pt If the truck has factory lockers, test them in low range on a loose surface (Slee). Water in the gear oil means bad breathers or seals.

Moly grease in the birfields, MP grease in the wheel bearings Pull the square knuckle fill plug. Runny grease means diff oil is getting past the inner axle seals (Slee). See the knuckle rebuild above for preload specs.
DEXRON-III ATF Persistent leaks are often the reservoir seals, not the box or the hoses (Unsealed 4X4).

DOT 3 hydraulic brake fluid (AMSOIL application guide) Slee reports front pads lasting about 10–15k miles (1997 pads last longer). If the truck has been lifted, the load-sensing proportioning valve needs readjusting.
1FZ accessory belts
MP grease at every zerk, including the slip yokes Overland Tailor's IH8MUD write-up blames most 80 Series driveline vibrations and clunks on driveshafts that were never serviced.
OEM fuel filter · PCV valve

J100 UZJ100 2UZ-FE 100 Series Land Cruiser underneath, with the 4.7-liter 2UZ-FE V8 and hydraulic Adjustable Height Control (AHC) suspension. A 100 Series Land Cruiser with a hydraulic party trick: it rises on its toes to clear a rock, then kneels so you can load the groceries. Keep up with the AHC fluid and the timing belt and it may well outlast the people who sold it new.

A harsh or bouncy ride, dark or metallic-gray fluid in the reservoir, sluggish leveling, or a flush that's overdue (owners say Lexus recommends one every 60k miles). 10 mm wrench · clear tubing · catch bottle · fluid evacuator or turkey baster · penetrating oil · Toyota AHC fluid 08886-01805
You want more ground clearance in Normal without giving up AHC. 10 mm socket · cut-off wheel · aluminum flat stock · drill · AHC fluid · tape measure

t: Timing belt, water pump and 90k service
x: The mileage says 90k, 180k or 270k with no proof the belt was done, or there's a weeping water pump or a rough idler bearing. ¾-in breaker bar · crank-pulley holder and puller · seal puller · thread locker · FIPG · drain pan · FSM
Clicking or no-crank conditions that come and go and get worse until it won't start. Long extensions · magnetic pickup · 22 mm wrench (fuel line) · new intake gaskets · rags

A tick-tick-pop at cold start that can sound like an exhaust leak, a misfire or coil failure. In the worst case a plug blows out of the head and takes the threads with it. Spark plug socket · extensions · torque wrench (in-lb and ft-lb) · compressed air · plugs · coil boots
A tick from the engine bay that's loudest cold and fades as the manifold heats and expands. Penetrating oil · stud extractor · engine support or jack · new gaskets and studs

Power-steering fluid leaking from the rack boots, play in the steering or a heavy feel. Long extensions · universal joints · 17 mm line wrench · metric sockets · new oil-filter-housing gasket · rack bushings

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The IH8MUD 100 Series FAQ answer is 285/75R16 or 285/65R18, both about 33 in, with no lift. An owner with a stock '99 found 295/75R16 a tight fit that might not clear at full bump and full lock. Stock sizes were 16-in wheels to 2002 and 275/60R18 from 2003.

t: How much can an LX 470 tow?
x: 6,500 lb with the towing package.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: The EPA rates a 2002 truck (four-speed) at 12 city, 15 highway and 13 combined. Five-speed trucks are rated 12 city, 15–16 highway and 13 combined. All run on regular fuel.

t: Is it a timing belt or a chain?
x: A belt. The 2UZ-FE is due every 90k miles. Owners replace the water pump, idlers, tensioner and thermostat at the same time, and often the starter or its contacts too, since the intake is already half apart.

If it's healthy, yes. It gives you adjustable ground clearance a spring truck can't match, and a fluid flush is a one-hour job. Owners whose AHC failed have switched to conventional suspension instead. One IH8MUD member went to Old Man Emu 2.5-in heavy springs and called it much cheaper than replacing AHC sensors and actuators, which another member described as very expensive.

t: How do I lift an LX 470?
x: The cheapest way is to adjust the AHC height-sensor links. That gives about 2 in up front (2.5 in with a trimmed heim joint) and about 1.75 in at the rear, or more with an extended bracket. Keep at least 70 mm of front droop for CV boot life, add a diff drop and get an alignment. The other route is removing the AHC and fitting conventional torsion bars, springs and shocks.

US trucks have a lockable center differential, plus brake-based A-TRAC from 2000. A factory rear locker was only offered on Canadian LX 470s in 1998–1999. Aftermarket air lockers are the usual upgrade.

Forum regulars favor 2000 and later for the stronger 4-pinion front differential, and 2003 and later for the A750F five-speed, which one member says makes a big difference. The 2006–2007 trucks add VVT-i and more power. The 2003–2007 trucks should also have had the steering-shaft recall done.

t: What's different from a 100 Series Land Cruiser?
x: The LX has the same drivetrain but different styling and equipment. It had AHC and AVS standard from 1998 (the Land Cruiser only got AHC as an option in 2006), front and rear automatic climate control, a power tilt and telescoping column, projector lows and fogs, body cladding and its own gauges and wheels.

t: Are there recalls I should check?
x: Yes. The big one is the July 2010 recall of about 39,000 2003–2007 LX 470s, which replaced the steering-shaft snap ring and added a retainer. There was also a 2004 US recall that added a resistor to dim daytime running lights that were too bright. In Australia, front rotor bolts and a dash wiring harness were recalled too.

t: What's that tick from the engine?
x: It could be either of two common 2UZ problems. A cracked driver's-side exhaust manifold ticks when cold and fades as it warms. A spark plug working loose makes a similar sound and is far more dangerous, because it can blow out of the head. IH8MUD members recommend checking the plugs first.

t: Suspension & Ahc — Metal Tech 4x4 (100 Series / LX 470 rear links), Old Man Emu
x: Adjust the AHC sensors for a lift, refresh the fluid and globes, or convert to conventional springs. Whichever route you take, adjustable rear links keep the rear axle centered once the truck is lifted.

t: Rock Sliders — Metal Tech 4x4 (100 Series / LX 470 sliders), Slee Off-Road
x: The cladding and running boards are expensive to replace. Sliders that bolt to the frame protect the rockers and can still work as steps.

t: Bumpers & Swing-Outs — Dissent Off-Road (LC100 / LX 470), Slee Off-Road
x: A modular front bumper protects the radiator and carries a winch, which matters on a truck this heavy. A rear bumper with swing-outs moves the spare up and out of the way.

t: Skid Plates — Dissent Off-Road (LC100 skids), Slee Off-Road
x: The IFS front differential and the transfer case sit low and exposed.
The stock intake is in the passenger fender. On US-spec trucks Slee notes the power antenna has to be swapped for a whip antenna.

t: Maintenance Parts — Cruiser Corps (100 Series), Cruiser Outfitters
x: Timing-belt kits, idlers, cam seals and plugs, stocked by people who know the chassis.

t: Timing belt, water pump, idlers & tensioner
x: Timing belt 13568-09070 per IH8MUD's 90k list (check for supersessions) Owners add the thermostat, cam and crank seals, and often the starter, which is easier to reach at this point in the job.
≈ 8 qt with filter (IH8MUD 90k list) · grade [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · filter 90915-YZZD3 IH8MUD notes a larger JDM-spec filter is available as an alternative to YZZD3.
17801-50040 per IH8MUD 90k list
UZJ100/LX470 element IH8MUD has an LX470 cabin filter DIY.
Iridium plugs, 8 (Denso SK20R11 or NGK IFR6A11, gap 1.0–1.1 mm, per the 2UZ-FE repair manual) · torque 13–15 ft-lb (17.5–20 N·m) 2UZ plugs can walk out and blow out of the head. Don't use anti-seize.

Toyota AHC fluid 08886-01805 · about 2 cans for a full flush Empty the reservoir in Low, then bleed each corner until clean fluid comes out (see the repair above). Compare reservoir levels in High and Low to judge the globes.
Pink Super Long Life Coolant, premixed (2004+). Earlier trucks were originally on a 30k / 2-yr coolant. Replace the brittle plastic heater-hose tees with metal ones before they crack (IH8MUD FAQ).

A343F (1998–2002): ATF T-IV [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]. A750F 2004+: ATF WS only, which isn't interchangeable. From 2004 there's no dipstick. Level is checked at the overflow plug (Slee). One owner reports about 6 qt per drain-and-fill. Repeat rather than flush.
GL-5 75W-90 · ≈ 1.3–1.4 qt Full is level with the bottom of the fill hole. Plug gaskets are 90430-18008 (IH8MUD).

SAE 90 in warm climates or 80W-90 in cooler ones (FSM, quoted on IH8MUD) · front under 2 qt Pull the fill plug first. The front uses a 10 mm Allen, the rear a 24 mm plug. Rear plugs are 35 ft-lb on 2002 FSM spec. A forum veteran says US 1998–99 LXs have a limited-slip rear [CONFIRM LSD ADDITIVE NEED IN MANUAL]. Clogged diff breathers are common.
MP grease at every zerk Owners say shops often skip the front shaft zerk hidden above the skid plate. Drop the skid and grease it.
OEM belt 90916-02586 per IH8MUD 90k list

Fluid type per reservoir cap [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] The brake system uses a high-pressure pump and accumulator, not a vacuum booster. Follow the IH8MUD brake-flush procedure and take any ABS/BRAKE warning seriously.
UZJ100/LX470 fuel filter · PCV valve (1998–07/2002 part shown)

J200 URJ200 3UR-FE The 200 Series twin, powered by the 5.7-liter 3UR-FE V8 (383 hp in US/Canada trim). Nearly three tons of hydraulically levitated V8 that Car and Driver called the most desirable SUV on the planet. The punchline is that a used one often costs less than the Land Cruiser it's built on.

A wet line or pink crust along the top plastic tank next to the molded platform, slow coolant loss and a sweet smell after a drive. It's most often reported on 2008–2010 trucks. Basic metric sockets · drain pan · hose pliers · Toyota Super Long Life Coolant · new radiator (later part number)

Pink crust or drips around the water pump weep hole at the front of the engine. It's commonly reported on 2008 trucks. Metric sockets · fan clutch wrench · drain pan · new pump and gasket · Toyota SLLC

Pink coolant dripping from the top of the transmission hump at the back of the engine, with the water pump area dry. Long extensions · swivel sockets · gasket scraper · grey FIPG · union pipe O-rings · new intake gaskets

A clunk or 'thunk' when pulling away or stopping, driveline vibration and dry slip yokes. 12 mm and 14 mm sockets · 14 mm wrench · extensions · torque wrench · pry bar · paint pen · grease gun with MP grease

A sudden no-crank, usually with no warning. The failure is typically in the solenoid, the high-current relay built onto the back of the starter. Metric sockets · long extensions · battery terminal wrench · new or reman starter
Service interval due (one high-mileage owner did his at 120k miles), misfires or rough idle. Spark plug socket · extensions · torque wrench · compressed air · OEM-spec plugs
Wet hydraulic fluid at line junctions or actuators, uneven leveling, a sagging corner or a harsh ride. Flashlight · mirror · Techstream-capable scan tool · factory repair manual

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The stock size is 285/50R20. The practical limit is about 33 in, and even that meant moving the front fender liner forward about an inch on one IH8MUD member's LX. His 35x12.5R20 build needed the liner moved further, the sidestep return trimmed and the body mount reshaped, with spacers giving about +35 mm effective offset. The LX is easier to fit than a Land Cruiser because it doesn't have the KDS

t: How much can an LX 570 tow?
x: Up to 8,500 lb at launch. The 2016-on owner's manual lists 7,000 lb (with trailer brakes) for the facelifted truck, so check the manual for your year. The hitch receiver is built into the frame.

t: What fuel economy should I expect, and does it need premium?
x: Yes, the EPA lists premium fuel. The six-speed 2008 is rated 12 city, 18 highway and 14 combined. The eight-speed 2016 is rated 13 city, 18 highway and 15 combined.

The US LX 570 has a lockable Torsen center differential plus A-TRAC, Crawl Control and, from 2013, Multi-Terrain Select. It has no factory front or rear axle lockers. Owners who want them fit aftermarket units such as ARB Air Lockers.

t: Is the AHC going to bankrupt me?
x: Probably not, if you buy a healthy one. One long-time IH8MUD poster wrote that after ten years in service the LX 570's AHC had turned out to be well engineered, without the expected horror stories. But leaks at line junctions and actuators are expensive, so inspect the system carefully before you buy.

They share the same frame, V8, transmission and transfer case. The LX swaps coil springs and KDSS for AHC, adds more luxury equipment and 20-in wheels, and over time got its own styling, with unique front and rear ends from 2016. DrivingLine noted that used LX 570s were typically priced below comparable Land Cruisers.

The 2008–2010 trucks have the most radiator-crack reports, and owners say 2008s had water-pump issues. The 2013–2015 trucks add Multi-Terrain Select and Turn Assist. The 2016 and later trucks get the eight-speed and a new interior. There is no 2012 model year in the US.

t: Is it a timing belt or a chain?
x: A chain. The 3UR-FE is a chain-driven DOHC V8, so there's no 90k belt service like the LX 470's.
Not in the US. Production of the 2011 model ran late and the 2013 started early, so the 2012 model year was skipped.

t: What does Crawl Control actually do?
x: It works like an off-road cruise control. It controls throttle and brakes to hold a slow, steady speed over obstacles, forward or in reverse. From 2013 you can choose from five speeds, and Turn Assist brakes the inside rear wheel to tighten low-range turns.

t: Rock Sliders — Metal Tech 4x4 (LX 570 sliders), Slee Off-Road
x: The aluminum running boards and AHC lines live along the rockers. Real sliders protect both.

t: Bumpers & Swing-Outs — Dissent Off-Road (LX570 front, LC200/LX570 rear), Slee Off-Road
x: The LX has its own front end, so it needs an LX-specific front bumper. The rear is shared with the Land Cruiser.

t: Skid Plates & Guards — BudBuilt (LC200 / LX570 cat guard), Slee Off-Road
x: The factory plastic won't stop a rock. Bash plates and a catalytic-converter guard protect the expensive parts underneath.

t: Rear Links — Metal Tech 4x4 (200 Series / LX570 links)
x: Adjustable links let you re-center the rear axle and correct pinion angle once ride height changes.
US trucks came without axle lockers. Air lockers add front and rear locking without touching the AHC.
Nearly three tons of truck needs a winch on a proper bumper and recovery points rated for the job.

t: Early differential, transfer case and transmission fluid service
x: None. This is preventive work. Some owners choose to change gear oil early after reports of debris in V35A Tundra differentials after break-in. Socket set · fluid pump · drain pan · torque wrench · gear oil per factory spec · grease gun

The factory underbody protection on most LX 600s isn't trail-ready. The LX 700h Overtrail is the exception, with a steel skid from the factory. Floor jack · sockets · torque wrench · skid plate kit (e.g. Slee Off-Road)
Delayed or missing throttle response pulling out of a rolling stop on 2024 trucks. Owners say it's worse in Sport and Sport+. None
Not a fault. The factory 22s limit you to low-profile tires that dislike rocks. Lug wrench · torque wrench · hub-centric wheels in the right offset · TPMS sensors

A squeal from the front brakes when moving forward or in reverse. Owners mostly hear it on the first stops of a cold or humid morning, and it fades once the brakes warm up. Lug wrench · socket set · torque wrench · brake cleaner · high-temperature brake grease · pads and rotors

t: Windshield rattle or buzz at speed (bulletin L-SB-0019-24)
x: A rattle or buzz from the windshield's outer edge molding above about 55 mph. Separately, owners chasing a rattle at the lower driver's-side corner of the windshield found leaves trapped near the hood hinge and in the wiper well. Shop vacuum · flashlight · trim tools if you inspect the molding yourself

t: Power back door won't close (pinch sensor)
x: The hatch opens normally, but when you press close it beeps once or twice and won't move, so you have to shut it by hand. The hands-free kick sensor may only beep. Key fob · Lexus dealer for sensor diagnosis

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The factory size on 22s is 265/50R22, about 32 in. Owners on aftermarket 20s run 275/60R20 (about 33 in) and 285/55R20 without rubbing, and 275/70R18 fits on Toyota TRD 18-inch wheels. 285/50R22 on factory wheels needed cutting and spacers. Without a lift, plan on about 33 in.

t: Is my LX 600 part of the engine recall?
x: If it's a 2022–2024, possibly. Recall 24V-381 covered 3,524 LX 600s built from July 30, 2021 to November 25, 2022, with engine replacement as the remedy. Recall 25V-767 (Lexus 25LA07) covers 9,895 LXs built from February 26, 2022 to April 2, 2024. Check your VIN at lexus.com/recall or nhtsa.gov. The 25V-767 remedy is a No. 1 main-bearing inspection, with engine replacement if needed.
8,000 lb with trailer brakes, per the owner's manual (1,650 lb without). KBB lists the same 8,000-lb rating for every 2027 LX.

t: Is the LX 600 just a 300 Series Land Cruiser?
x: Underneath, yes: same GA-F platform and 112-in wheelbase. Toyota didn't sell the LC300 in North America, which made the LX 600 the US version.

There's a lockable center diff, but no US LX 600 has front or rear lockers. The F Sport gets a Torsen limited-slip rear. Triple locks came on Japan's LX Offroad grade and, in the US, on the LX 700h Overtrail.

t: How do I use 4L and the diff locks?
x: Owners say the center diff lock can be engaged while moving slowly in Drive. Shifting into 4L requires the truck to be stopped and in neutral. On trucks with axle lockers, the front and rear lockers need 4L and the center lock engaged first, at very low speed. If you switch off the engine in 4L, MTS won't come back on automatically.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: The EPA rates the 2025 LX 600 at 17 mpg city, 22 highway and 19 combined, on premium fuel.

t: How much lighter is it than the LX 570?
x: Lexus says 441 lb (200 kg) lighter, with a frame it calls 20 percent more rigid.
At normal ride height, 25° approach, 23° breakover and 20° departure. Lexus hasn't published figures for the Hi1 and Hi2 heights. Maximum wading depth is 700 mm (27.5 in).

t: Why does it clunk into first gear?
x: Owners report a clunk into first on rolling stops, and sometimes on 6–5 downshifts, in 2022–2024 LX 600s. There's no known fix. Gentle throttle while the transmission decides helps, and larger tires make it less noticeable. Owners say the LX 700h hybrid doesn't do it.

t: Should I buy one without AHC?
x: If you plan to lift it, maybe. Slee Off-Road's LX 600 build was a Premium custom-ordered without AHC so it could run Dobinsons suspension. AHC trucks keep the adjustable ride heights but limit your lift choices.

t: Rear air spring replacement or coil conversion

No symptoms until it fails, which is the problem. Due every 90,000 miles. The water pump is belt-driven, so a weeping pump or coolant crust behind the timing covers is a good reason to do both now. t: Exhaust manifold replacement (often the driver's side)
x: A ticking noise from the engine bay that is loudest cold and often fades as the manifold heats and expands. The cause is a paper-thin crack where the flange meets the first pipe. Engine support or jack · penetrating oil · stud extractor set · new manifold, gaskets, studs and nuts

Wet rack boots, a falling power-steering reservoir, and creaking or whining on every turn of the wheel. Tie-rod end puller · flare-nut wrenches · drain pan · ATF/PS fluid · OEM reman rack (e.g. CVJ or Cardone) · new rack bushings

t: Front lower ball joints and control arms
x: Torn ball-joint boots weeping grease, clunks over bumps, and vague steering. Worn lower control arm bushings add knocks of their own. Ball-joint press · pickle fork or joint separator · torque wrench · grease gun · lower control arm or ball joint
Grease slung around the inside of the wheel, split CV boots, and clicking on tight turns. Large axle-nut socket · breaker bar · pry bar · joint separator · torque wrench · new axle nut and OEM axle

Usually nothing until it breaks. A 'vacuum cleaner' whine for about 30 seconds after a cold start that gets rougher as the pump fails. Owners report codes including P2440, P2442, P2445 and P2432, and one reported random limp mode. t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The stock size is 265/65R17. On a stock or nearly stock GX 470, the safe consensus is about 31.5 inches. Owners report 265/70R17 working with little or no rubbing (one reports a slight rub at full lock in reverse), and 255/75R17 with zero rubbing. Going to 33 inches (285/70R17, or the narrower 255/80R17) generally means a 2–3 in lift and some liner trimming.

t: How much can a GX 470 tow?
x: 2003 models are rated for 5,000 lb. Midway through the 2004 model year, Lexus fitted a stronger frame-bolted tubular hitch and raised the rating to 6,500 lb.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: The EPA rates it at 14 mpg city, 18 highway and 15 combined (2007), and it calls for premium fuel. Bigger tires typically cost owners another 1 to 1.5 mpg.

t: Is it a timing belt or a chain?
x: It's a belt. Toyota's interval for UZ V8s is 90,000 miles, and the belt drives the water pump, so most owners replace both together.

t: What fluids and capacities does it take?
x: Per the 2005 factory repair manual: engine oil 5W-30, 6.5 US qt (6.2 L) with filter. The A750F automatic takes Toyota Genuine ATF WS only, about 3.2 qt (3.0 L) per drain-and-fill and 11.0 qt (10.4 L) dry. Transfer case: 1.5 qt (1.4 L, about 3 pints) of GL-5 75W-90. Front diff 1.48 qt (1.40 L) and rear diff 3.22 qt (3.05 L), both GL-5 SAE 90 (80W-90 below 0°F). Coolant is about 13.6 qt (12.9 L) of

t: When should I lock the center diff?
x: Lock it whenever you're off pavement with loose traction. Many owners leave it locked for all trail driving, because it cuts down how much A-TRAC has to work on climbs. Unlock it for very tight turns on grippy surfaces and back on pavement. VSC is disabled while the center diff is locked.

t: Should I keep the rear air suspension?
x: It works well while healthy, and Expedition Portal's build kept it for load leveling. But aging bags leak where they fold over rusty perches, compressors wear out chasing those leaks, and a failure can leave you on the bump stops. Many owners convert to coils for well under the cost of new air parts.

t: How do I tell if a GX 470 has KDSS?
x: Watch for a momentary KDSS light when you turn the key, or look for the noticeably large front sway bar. It was optional from late in the 2004 model year. It helps both stability and articulation, but it complicates some armor installs.

2005 and later get the VVT-i engine (rated 270 hp, then restated as 263 hp from 2006). Trucks from mid-2004 on get the 6,500 lb hitch. 2008–2009 trucks have the facelift. In practice, condition beats model year: rust, timing-belt records, air suspension, steering rack and manifold matter more than the build date.

Common choices are Icon's 0–3.5 in systems (sold by Metal Tech 4x4), ToyTec kits, and Old Man Emu BP-51 coilovers, which Expedition Portal used. ARB doesn't list the GX as an approved application, so check warranty terms first. Pair any front lift with a rear coil conversion or an air spacer to level it.

Not quite. It's a Land Cruiser Prado 120 underneath. The 4th-gen 4Runner shares its suspension layout and was built on the same Tahara line, so many parts and much of the forum knowledge carry across. The GX had the V8 and full-time 4WD with a center lock as standard.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: The EPA rates the 2010 GX 460 at 15 mpg city, 20 highway and 17 combined, and the 2023 at 15/19/16, on premium fuel. It's a 5,100-plus-lb truck with a V8, so bigger tires and roof racks pull that down.

t: Which trims have rear air suspension?
x: The 2010–2013 Premium, and the 2014-on Luxury, which is the equivalent trim after the reshuffle. Those trucks also get AVS adaptive dampers. Lifting one means converting the rear to coils first.

t: Can I add Crawl Control or Multi-Terrain Select?
x: Yes, on 2010–2019 trucks of any trim, using factory switch panels and a zero-point calibration. Part numbers differ by year and by whether the truck still has AVS/RAHC. Retrofit details for 2020-on trucks are unknown.
Yes. KDSS is standard, so buy KDSS-specific front skids (ARB and ASFIR both make versions). Expect some lean after a rear coil conversion. Southern Style Offroad's kit includes spacers to correct it.

t: Which years should I buy or avoid?
x: 2010–2013 trucks have the air-pump issue (confirm the updated parts or warranty work). 2014-on trucks get the spindle-grille facelift. 2020-on Off-Road package trucks have Crawl Control, MTS and a transmission cooler from the factory. 2022–2023 trucks add CarPlay. Mechanically, Lexus changed little, so condition and records matter more than year.

t: What was the Consumer Reports 'Don't Buy' about?
x: In April 2010, the stability control was slow to catch a lift-off oversteer slide. Toyota recalled the trucks for a VSC software update, and Consumer Reports lifted the label on May 7, 2010.

The core drivetrain has a good reputation. The well-documented failures are leaks and accessories: water pumps, the coolant valley, the timing cover, early air pumps and, on some trucks, the cold-start P2714/P0761 shift fault. Budget for those, and a 200k-mile GX 460 is not unusual.

Often, yes. IH8MUD's build guide notes that 5th-gen 4Runner KDSS-compatible front skids and gas-tank skids usually swap over, and some 4th-gen V8 4Runner transmission and transfer-case skids have been used. Bumpers and body parts are GX-specific.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?

t: Is my GX 550 part of the engine recall?
x: Possibly, if it's a 2024. Recall 25V-767 (Lexus 25LA07) covers 3,717 US-market 2024 GXs built between May 31, 2023 and April 10, 2024, for machining debris that can damage the engine. Check your VIN at lexus.com/recall or nhtsa.gov. The remedy is a No. 1 main-bearing inspection, with engine replacement if needed.

t: What does the Overtrail get that other grades don't?
x: An electronically locking rear differential, E-KDSS that disconnects the anti-roll bars, standard 33-inch A/T tires on 18s, and a wider body. Seven seats are listed only for the non-Overtrail grades.

It's full-time 4WD on every GX 550, with a Torsen limited-slip center differential that locks and splits torque 50:50. A two-speed transfer case gives you low range. Multi-Terrain Select offers Auto, Sand, Mud and Rock in low range, and Auto, Dirt, Sand, Mud and Deep Snow in high. Crawl Control works in low range at five speeds.

t: Is it a Land Cruiser underneath?
x: Yes. It shares the GA-F platform with the Land Cruiser Prado, sold in the US as the Land Cruiser 250, and with the LX 600. The GX was revealed first, on June 8, 2023.
Lexus quotes up to 26° approach, 24° breakover and 21° departure.
At launch, Lexus said a hybrid powertrain would come to the US later. US GX 550s use the 3.4-liter twin-turbo V6.

t: V6 or the old V8: which is stronger?
x: On paper, the V6. It makes 349 hp and 479 lb-ft, compared with 301 hp and 329 lb-ft from the GX 460's 4.6 V8. The V8's advantage is its long track record, while the V35A is still early in its story and has had recalls.

t: What oil does it take, and how much?
x: Lexus's owner's manual calls for ILSAC GF-6A 0W-20 and lists 7.7 qt with a new filter (7.4 qt without). 5W-20 is allowed only as a stopgap until the next change. The standard interval is 10,000 miles or 12 months, or 6 months / 5,000 miles if you mostly drive dirt or dusty roads, make short trips below freezing, or idle a lot.

Planned as a long shot, it won Paris–Dakar at its third attempt and kicked off Japan's RV boom. In America it was a Montero or a Dodge Raider. Either way you get a simple torsion-bar 4x4 with an inclinometer on the dash and a lot

t: Inspect the pitman-arm ball joint and steering boots
x: Wander, play at the wheel, or split ball-joint boots. Mitsubishi Japan's notice lists every first-generation code (L041G–L149G). It warns that on old, hard-used trucks with integral ball-nut steering, a corroded pitman-arm ball joint can break and cause loss of steering. Jack and stands · ball-joint separator · torque wrench · grease gun · molybdenum-disulfide chassis grease.

A chain rattle from the front of the engine, worst at cold start. The 4G54 has Mitsubishi's 'Silent Shaft' twin balance shafts, and aftermarket timing kits for the Montero's 4G54 include two chains, tensioners and guides. Factory service manual · crank-pulley holder and puller · torque wrench · gasket scraper · RTV and new gaskets.

t: Fuel pump, filter and the 'won't stay running' fix
x: Hard hot starts, stumbling or dying under load. Several Bring a Trailer sellers list a replaced fuel pump and filter in recent work on 2.6 Raiders and Monteros. Line wrenches · hose clamps · fuel-rated hose · fire extinguisher · a pressure gauge if you have one.

t: Set the front ride height at the torsion bars
x: A nose-down stance, or one front corner lower than the other. Like every Pajero up to 1999, the first generation has double-wishbone front suspension on torsion bars. Jack and stands · tape measure · socket and long extension · anti-seize.

t: Rear drum brakes and wheel cylinders
x: A spongy pedal, fluid on the inside of the rear tyre, or pulling under braking. US Raiders and Monteros on Bring a Trailer have front discs and rear drums, and one seller replaced the wheel cylinders along with the shocks and idler arm. Brake-spring tool · flare-nut wrench · bleeder hose · DOT 3 fluid.

t: Check the automatic locking hubs and part-time 4WD
x: 4WD that won't engage or won't release. US trucks have automatically locking front hubs as standard. Mitsubishi says the first generation's part-time system binds ('tight-corner braking') if you use 4WD on dry pavement. Snap-ring pliers · hub socket · wheel-bearing grease · factory manual.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: We couldn't find a clear forum consensus for the first generation. Documented examples include a BaT 1990 Montero LS on 285/70R17 tyres (about 33 inches) on aftermarket 17-inch wheels; the listing doesn't mention a lift. Most first-generation trucks run 15-inch wheels. Measure your clearance at full lock and full stuff before you buy tyres.

t: Is the Dodge Raider the same as the Montero?
x: Yes. It's the three-door Pajero/Montero, built by Mitsubishi and sold by Dodge from 1987 to 1989, with the 2.6 four and, from 1988, the 3.0 V6. Dodge never sold the five-door.

t: Did the Pajero really win the Dakar?
x: Yes. Patrick Zaniroli and Jean Da Silva won the 1985 rally overall, with Andrew Cowan second. It was the first overall win for a Japanese manufacturer, but the winning car was a works prototype. A production-based Pajero won its class on the 1983 debut, and Cowan was third overall in 1984.

t: Can I drive it in 4WD on the road?
x: No. The first generation has part-time 4WD with no centre differential. Mitsubishi itself names tight-corner binding on pavement as the system's weakness, and it's why Super Select was developed for the second generation. Use 4WD on loose or slippery surfaces only.

t: Which engine should I look for?
x: In the US: the 2.6 four (109 hp) or, from 1988, the 3.0 V6 (143 hp). The V6 is the better highway engine. Japanese and European imports may have the 2.5 4D56 turbo-diesel, which got an intercooler in 1988 and uses a timing belt.

On Bring a Trailer since 2024, US Monteros and Raiders have sold for $3,850 to $24,000. Clean, original V6 LS trucks are at the top, and Raiders have sold between $5,100 and $11,300. Imported Pajeros (2.5 turbo-diesels and V6s) have sold for about $3,850 to $16,250 on BaT since 2021.
The name comes from the Pampas cat, Leopardus pajeros. Mitsubishi used Montero in North America, Spain and most of Latin America because the word is a crude insult in Spanish, and Shogun in the UK.

t: Can I import a diesel or JDM first-generation Pajero to the US?
x: Yes. Every first-generation truck is now more than 25 years old, which meets NHTSA's exemption. The EPA rules are separate: the vehicle must be in original configuration (or have an equivalent EPA-certified engine). Then check your state's titling rules.

t: What's the gauge pod on the dash?
x: An inclinometer, flanked by a voltmeter and an oil-pressure gauge. Interior designer Hiroshi Mizutani modelled it on aircraft and crane controls and believes it was the first three-dimensional inclinometer in a production car.

Early trucks have leaf-sprung rear axles. Long-wheelbase trucks switched to three-link coil springs in 1988; short-wheelbase US trucks such as BaT's 1988 Montero Sport kept leaves. Check under the truck before you order springs or shocks.

t: Oem & Service Parts — RockAuto — 1989 Montero 2.6, RockAuto — 1989 Montero 3.0 V6, RockAuto — 1988 Dodge Raider 2.6
x: Filters, steering joints, brakes and hub parts for US trucks, sorted by engine. Raider parts are the same as the Montero's.

t: Timing Chain Kits — FridayParts — 4G54 timing chain kit
x: A two-chain kit (timing and balance shaft) with guides and tensioners is the standard cure for a rattling 4G54.
Practical upgrades for Raiders and first-generation Monteros, including an electric fuel pump conversion.
5W-30 or 10W-30 grades listed by temperature · ≈5.5 US qt with filter (2.6) AMSOIL lists a WIX 51381 filter for the 2.6.
4G54 2.6: chains (timing and balance shaft) · 4D56 2.5 TD: belt On a diesel import with no records, assume the belt is due.

[CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Old rubber fuel hose is a fire risk; replace it with fuel-rated hose.

V20 V40 V55W Evolution Montero Shogun Super Select 4WD, 6G72 and 6G74 V6s, 4D56 and 4M40 diesels, an optional rear locker and the Dakar-bred Pajero Evolution. The Pajero grew up: Super Select let you leave it in four-wheel drive on the highway, the V6s made it quick, and the Evolution made it faintly ridiculous. Keep the timing belt fresh and the cooling system honest and it's as tough as its Daka

t: Timing belt, tensioner and water pump (6G72 3.0 / 6G74 3.5)
x: Usually none before it fails. A whirring from the belt area can mean an over-tight belt or a failing idler. Australian owners change it about every 100,000 km and warn that the 3.5 has no valve clearance if the belt breaks, while the 3.0 does. Treat those as owner reports and check your engine. Crank-pulley holding tool · torque wrench (inch-pound range) · vice to reset the hydraulic tensioner · p

t: Cure a flashing 4WD light (front axle engagement)
x: The Super Select lights keep flashing after you select 4H, or the front axle never engages. Owners say the system 'sometimes plays up if not used very much'. Hand vacuum pump with gauge · multimeter · basic hand tools · replacement vacuum hose.

t: Inspect the pitman-arm ball joint (Mitsubishi's procedure)
x: Steering play, a clunk through the wheel, or a split ball-joint boot. Mitsubishi Japan warns that on old, hard-used trucks with integral ball-nut steering, corrosion and wear can break the pitman-arm ball joint and cause loss of steering. Every second-generation chassis code, the V55W Evolution included, is on its list. Jack and stands · ball-joint separator or hammer · torque wrench · grease gun

t: Reset or upgrade the front torsion bars
x: The nose sits low. One ExplorOz contributor says many high-mileage Pajeros 'almost look like they're sitting on the front bump stops.' A heavy steel bull bar makes it worse. Jack and stands · tape measure · socket set for the adjusters · alignment afterwards.

t: V6 head gasket replacement (and do it properly)
x: Coolant loss, milky oil on the dipstick or under the filler cap, overheating. One NJ 3.0 owner on ExplorOz had replaced the head gasket twice in about three years. Mechanics in that thread say the V6s have a weak spot for head gaskets and that the heads 'do crack a fair bit'. Factory manual · 1/2-in torque wrench · straight edge and feeler gauges · machine shop for crack test and skim · labelled b

Cracked, chafed or weeping front hoses. NHTSA recall 96V143 says the wheel-side front hoses on 1992–94 Monteros could crack at full steering lock and full suspension travel. Recall 98V220 covers 1997–98 front brake lines chafing through at the inner-fender pass-through. Flare-nut wrenches · hose clamp · new copper washers · bleeder hose and bottle · DOT 3 fluid.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: We found no single forum consensus, but the evidence points to about 31 inches. An Australian owner lists the 1996 NL GLX's stock tyres as 235/75R15 on 15x6 steel wheels and calls 31x10.5R15 'a good tyre size'. BaT's 1994 Montero SR runs 31x10.50R15s on its factory 15-inch alloys, and a 1995 Pajero sold on 265/70R16s. Go bigger and you'll want a lift, and probably some trimming.

t: Can I drive in 4WD on the highway?
x: Yes, in 4H. That's the point of Super Select: 4H is full-time 4WD with an open centre differential, so it doesn't bind on pavement. 4HLc and 4LLc lock the centre and are for loose surfaces only. You can move between 2H and 4H on the move.

A pneumatic rear locker was a factory option. It works only with the centre differential locked, in 4HLc or 4LLc. BaT's 1994 Montero SR and 1998 Montero both have locking rear differentials. Check the dash switch and the air lines before you assume a truck has one.

The 3.0 V6 is the common US engine. Australian owners say it has valve clearance if the belt breaks, but it's down on power. The 3.5 is the strong one: 215 hp in the DOHC US SR, 200 hp in the later SOHC Montero. Outside the US, the 4M40 2.8 turbo-diesel has a timing chain and a good reputation, but some owners report head problems. The 4D56 2.5 is slower and belt-driven.

Australian owners on ExplorOz say the 3.5 has no clearance if the belt breaks and the 3.0 does. Treat that as owner experience and confirm with the factory manual or a specialist. Either way, the belt is a scheduled part, so change it on time.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: Owners report about 13–14 L/100 km around town and about 11 on the highway from a 3.5 petrol, and 14 highway and 16 town from an NL GLS automatic. Towing pushes that to about 20. A 3.0 owner averaged 11.3 L/100 km. One owner towing almost constantly with a DOHC 3.5 saw 25–30 L/100 km. Diesels are 10–20% better, according to an owner who runs one.

t: Pajero, Montero or Shogun: what's the difference?
x: Just the name. Montero was used in North America, Spain and most of Latin America, because 'pajero' is a crude insult in Spanish. Shogun was the UK name. The name Pajero comes from the Pampas cat, Leopardus pajeros.

t: Can I import a Japanese-market Pajero or Evolution into the US?
x: Yes, if it's at least 25 years old, counted from its own build date. Every second-generation truck now qualifies. The EPA's exemption is separate: it needs the vehicle in original configuration (or with an equivalent EPA-certified engine) and at least 21 years old. State rules vary, and California is the hard one.
On Bring a Trailer, sold Evolutions from late 2024 to October 2026 ran from $19,500 to $49,997, with a median of about $32,000. Low-kilometre trucks and the rare five-speed manuals sit at the top.

Uprated torsion bars at the front and coils at the rear. Old Man Emu torsion bars for 1991-on Mitsubishis are sold in the US, and Dobinsons sells a 45 mm kit for the NH–NL Pajero. One Australian owner reported 65 mm of lift from a TJM kit. Owners say to match front and rear spring rates, and you'll need an alignment.

t: Are there safety recalls I should know about?
x: The big one is the NADI driver airbag: NHTSA 20V035000 for 1998–2000 Monteros, and a buy-back program for affected NL Pajeros in Australia, because no replacement inflator exists. Earlier trucks have brake-hose recalls (96V143, 98V220) and a 3.0 crank-pulley bolt recall (00V311001).

t: Suspension Lift — Old Man Emu, SuperSpares — Dobinsons 45 mm kit, Pajero NH–NL
x: Fresh torsion bars, rear coils and shocks fix the saggy nose and make room for 31s and up. Match the spring rates front to rear.

t: Uprated Torsion Bars — Hurreys Performance — ARB/OME torsion bar set, Mitsubishi 91+
x: The Pajero's front springs are its torsion bars. Uprated bars hold ride height under a bull bar and winch without cranking tired factory bars further.
