SJ410 SJ413 Samurai JA51 JB31 Leaf springs, a 1.3-litre G13 four and a 2,000-lb curb weight: the cult rock crawler that survived Consumer Reports. A 2,000-lb ladder-frame 4x4 that Consumer Reports said tipped over and the trail crowd says goes everywhere. Both had a point. Give it some lift, a locker and lower gears and it climbs things that embarrass trucks three times its size.

t: Rebuild the front knuckles (kingpins, seals, wheel bearings)
x: Gear oil weeping from the knuckle balls, loose or wandering steering, play when you rock the top of the tire, and grease or oil inside the brake parts. Socket set · seal driver · bearing packer · torque wrench · spring scale for kingpin preload · service manual

A clunk when you shift on and off the throttle, a transfer case that sags or rocks, a cracked mounting boss or a frame bracket starting to tear. Lower transfer-case gears make it worse. Jack and stands · welder and grinder · drill · socket set

t: Replace the transfer case shift sheet and seals
x: Sloppy or stiff transfer case lever, trouble finding 4WD or low, a case that pops out of gear, and leaks at the output seals. Socket set · seal puller and driver · gasket scraper · fluid pump

t: Rear wheel bearing and axle seal
x: Gear oil on the inside of the rear wheel or the brake shoes, a growl that changes with speed, or play in the rear wheel. Slide hammer · press or bearing shop · die grinder · brake bleeding kit

Unknown belt history, a cracked or glazed belt, or a noisy tensioner. The G13A is a non-interference engine, so a snapped belt strands you but shouldn't bend valves. Socket set · crank pulley holder · torque wrench · timing light
Slipping under load in low range, chatter, or a pedal that engages right at the top of its travel. Transmission jack · socket set · clutch alignment tool · torque wrench

t: Brake master cylinder and front brake refresh
x: A sinking pedal, fluid around the master cylinder or booster, and pulsing or noisy front brakes. Flare-nut wrenches · bench-bleed kit · brake bleeder · C-clamp

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: About a 215/75R15. On Zukiworld, owners say a 215/75R15 fits a stock Samurai with no modifications and 225s fit with a little effort. A 235/75R15 (about 29 inches) needs trimming and flattened inner fender seams, a 1.5–2 inch lift, or both. Stock tires were P205/70R15 according to the 1986 brochure.

t: Does the Samurai really roll over easily?
x: It depends who you ask. CU's 1988 'Not Acceptable' rating came from tip-ups in a severe, modified avoidance maneuver, and NHTSA denied petitions to investigate a defect. In the 2004 settlement CU said it never meant the Samurai easily rolls over in routine driving. NHTSA's Michigan data put its rollover rate close to the Wrangler's, but it's still short and narrow, so drive it like one.

1986–early 1988 trucks have the firmest ride and the tallest fifth gear (0.795). The '1988½' update brought softer springs, a thicker front anti-roll bar and a 0.865 fifth gear. 1990–95 trucks have throttle-body injection. Condition and the quality of past modifications matter more than the year.

t: What engine does it have, and what's the common swap?
x: The 1,324 cc SOHC eight-valve G13A (64 hp), then the injected G13BA. The common upgrade is a 1.6-litre Sidekick or Tracker engine, which bolts to the same mounts. Trail Tough sells kits for 1.6 and 2.0/2.3 Suzuki conversions. Check your state's emissions rules first.

t: Should I re-gear the transfer case or the axles?
x: Trail Tough's advice is to do both, in that order of importance: choose ring-and-pinion gears to suit the tire size, then pick transfer case gears for crawling. Doing all the reduction in the transfer case overloads the U-joints, the transfer case mounts and the frame brackets.

t: How much lift do I need for 29s, 31s or bigger?
x: Trail Tough rates the 2-inch Old Man Emu spring kit as 'just right for a 29-inch tire'. Its spring-over kit gives about 4.5 inches of lift for up to 31-inch tires. Bigger than that usually means a body lift, longer shackles, or a Toyota axle swap with custom steering.

t: Can I put Toyota axles under a Samurai?
x: Yes, and it's a very common swap. 1979–85 Toyota truck axles are about 5 inches wider than the Samurai's and take the same brake fittings. You need a way to deal with the different front spring perch width, flange adapters or redrilled flanges for the driveshafts, and aftermarket steering, because Samurai steering won't fit. Trail-Gear and Low Range Off-Road sell conversion kits.

t: Why does it grind or vibrate in 4WD high when it's lifted?
x: According to Trail Tough, the transfer case tilts down 7 degrees at the back while the front pinion points up about 9 degrees, so the front driveshaft's U-joint angles work against each other. Lift makes it worse. Tipping the pinion won't fix it, though a CV front driveshaft helps.

t: What fuel economy and tank range should I expect?
x: Suzuki's 1986 brochure quoted 27 mpg city and 29 highway (1986 EPA estimates) and a 40-litre (10.6 US gallon) tank. Real-world numbers fall with big tires and lift.

Trail Tough's Spartan automatic locker fits the rear of every Samurai and the front of 1986–89 trucks. ARB Air Lockers and spools are also available. Even an open front diff with a rear locker makes a big difference on the trail.
NHTSA lists one US campaign: 95V103008 for 1988–1991 Samurais, which covers front seat belt buckles whose red release buttons can break.

t: Suspension Lift — Trail Tough — Old Man Emu Samurai lift, Trail Tough — SPOA suspension system, Low Range Off-Road — spring over axle kit
x: An Old Man Emu spring-under kit adds about 2 inches for 29-inch tires. A spring-over (SPOA) conversion gives about 4.5 inches for 31s and is the classic Samurai trail build.

t: Transfer Case Gears — Trail Tough — 4.16 Sumo crawler gears, Trail Tough — 6.4 Sumo gears, Trail Tough — Mighty Kong II mount
x: Lower transfer case gears are the Samurai's signature crawling mod. Sumo 4.16:1 gears give 84 percent more low-range reduction, and 6.4:1 gears give 181 percent. Brace the case mounts when you fit them.

t: Axle Gears & Lockers — Trail Tough — Revolution Gear 4.57 / 5.38, Trail Tough — Spartan automatic locker, Trail Tough — ARB Air Locker
x: Regear the 6 7/8-inch Suzuki differentials for bigger tires, then lock them.

t: Axle Swap — Trail-Gear — Toyota leaf spring swap kit for Samurai (front), Trail Tough — Toyota to Samurai high-steer kit
x: Toyota axles are wider and stronger and have a deep aftermarket, which is why they're the standard upgrade for big tires.

t: Engine Swap — Trail Tough — 1.6 litre conversion kit, Trail Tough — 2.0/2.3 litre conversion kit
x: A 1.6 from a Sidekick or Tracker bolts to the same mounts. 2.0 and 2.3 conversions go further.

t: Steering — Trail Tough — knuckle-over steering, Trail Tough — rag joint eliminator
x: Knuckle-over steering puts the drag link above the springs and cures bump steer on spring-over trucks.

t: Armor & Bumpers — Trail Tough — full skid plate, Trail Tough — front winch bumper, Trail Tough — sport cage
x: Skid plates, sliders and tight-fitting bumpers protect a truck that spends its life on rocks.
3.9 qt with filter · 10W-30 or 10W-40 depending on temperature AMSOIL lists WIX 51348 as the matching filter.
G13A (1986–89) belt and tensioner The G13A is a non-interference engine (Wikipedia), so a failure shouldn't bend valves, but it will strand you.
1.3 8V plug wire set MotorTrend lists oil leaks at the distributor as a known trouble spot, so check the distributor O-ring while you're there.
Carbureted 1986–89; throttle-body injected 1990–95 A carburetor rebuild kit is available if the idle won't settle.
5.3 qt · coolant type [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Check the radiator, hoses and the 1.3 water inlet pipe.
2.7 pt · 75W-90 GL-4 Drain and fill plugs differ between 1986–88 and 1988.5–95 trucks.
1.7 pt · GL-4 per AMSOIL; Trail Tough fills its rebuilt cases with non-synthetic 80W-90 GL-5 While it's drained, check the case mounts and the shift sheet.

3.2 pt · GL-5 90 (1988) or 75W-90 (1992) With an automatic locker or spool, use the oil the locker maker specifies.
DOT 3 1986–89 trucks use their own master cylinder.
Dexron-III ATF (AMSOIL, 1988) Only applies if your truck has power steering.
Grease points [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] A seized steering joint and crumbling spring or body bushings are normal at this age.
Aisin manual hubs Lock and unlock both hubs. They must be locked for 4WD to work.

JB23 JB33 JB43 JB53 Twenty-year, coil-sprung, ladder-frame Jimny; 1998–2001 trucks are now 25-year legal to import to the US. A ladder frame, two live axles and a real low range, shrunk until it fits in a Japanese parking space and priced like a hatchback. The Jimny that ran for twenty years is the smallest proper 4x4 you can import, and its only natural predator is road salt.

t: Replace the kingpin bearings and halfshaft seal
x: Steering-wheel shake around 45–50 mph, play when you rock a raised wheel at 12 and 6 o'clock with the brakes held, and diff oil mixed with grease leaking from the swivel ball. A rusted-solid lower bearing can show no play at all. Jack and axle stands · torque wrench · bearing drift · gasket sealant · waterproof grease.

t: Chase down a death wobble that isn't the kingpins
x: Wobble remains after new kingpin bearings, or a sloppy, wandering feel at speed. Tie-rod end puller · bush press or drawbolt kit · wire brush for hub faces · alignment afterward.

t: Fix vacuum front hubs that won't engage
x: The 4WD light flashes, the front hubs don't click in, or 4WD works one day and not the next. Common on trucks that rarely use 4WD. 100 ml syringe · vacuum hose · basic hand tools.

On 2005-on trucks, the green 4WD light flashes (one owner counted 12 flashes) with a click, the 4L light may flash too, and 4WD won't engage even though the hubs lock when tested. Basic hand tools · contact cleaner · service manual for the actuator alignment procedure.

t: Repair rotten floors, sills and radius-arm brackets
x: Holes in the boot floor or under the rear seats, rust around the seat-belt anchors, MOT or inspection failures on body mounts, or a rear clunk from a corroded arm bracket. MIG welder · grinder · seam sealer · cavity wax and underbody coating.

t: Renew radius-arm bushes and check the axle mounts
x: A clunk when letting the clutch up, vague steering, or cracked and split bushes you can open with a screwdriver. Bush press or drawbolt set · straight edge · torque wrench.

Grinding or whining when cruising in 3rd or 4th on 2005-ish to 2008 petrol trucks, and a furry drain plug or metal chunks in the oil. Transmission jack · bearing pullers · impact sockets for pressing bearings · liquid gasket.

t: Change the G13BB timing belt (1998–2001 JB33)
x: No visible symptom until it snaps. It's a service item on early 1.3 Jimnys, which are exactly the trucks now eligible for US import. Timing marks and service manual · tensioner tools · coolant for the pump.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: Stock on the Wide/Sierra is 205/70R15 (about 27.1 inches). BigJimny's consensus is that 215/75R15 (about 27.7 inches) is the largest that fits an unmodified truck. 235/75R15 (about 28.8 inches) wants a 2-inch lift, and forum regulars say gen 3s still need some trimming even then, though a few owners run them with minor rubbing at full flex. Anything bigger than 215 really calls for regearing, or y

t: Can I legally import one to the US?
x: Yes, if it's at least 25 years old from its date of manufacture, which is the NHTSA exemption in 49 CFR 591.5(i). As of late 2026 that covers trucks built up to about October 2001: JB33 Wides, early JB43s and kei JB23s, plus the Mazda AZ-Offroad. Each later truck becomes eligible on its own 25th birthday. EPA has its own age-based exemption, and your state decides how it's titled.

t: What's the difference between JB23, JB33, JB43 and JB53?
x: JB23 is the Japanese kei car with the 658 cc turbo three and no fender flares. JB33 is the export 1.3 'Wide' with the G13BB. JB43 is the M13A-engined Wide or Sierra from 2000 to 2018. JB53 is the European diesel with Renault's 1.5 K9K. All four share the 2,250 mm wheelbase.

t: Which engine should I look for?
x: BigJimny rates both petrol engines as robust. The G13BB uses a timing belt with a 100,000 km interval, while the M13A uses a chain that doesn't need replacing. The M13A VVT (2005–06 on) is the strongest petrol at 85–86 PS, but its R72 gearbox had bearing problems in roughly 2005–2008 trucks. Avoid the early K9K 700 diesel, whose injection pump failures can wreck the engine.

t: Can I leave it in 4WD on the road?
x: No. There's no center differential, so 4WD on dry tarmac binds the driveline and can break CV joints, and Suzuki only sells the CV joint with the halfshaft. On push-button trucks, check you haven't knocked 4WD on by accident. Use 4WD on snow, mud, gravel, wet grass and sand.

t: How fast can I shift into 4WD?
x: The vacuum-locking front hubs let you go from 2WD to 4WD-High at up to 100 km/h (62 mph). Low range requires stopping, and on push-button trucks the clutch must be down with the gearbox in neutral.
A 2017 New Zealand-market Jimny Sierra was rated at 1,300 kg (2,866 lb) braked and 500 kg (1,102 lb) unbraked. Bear in mind that it only has 110 Nm of torque.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: Suzuki claimed 7.1 L/100 km combined for the 2017 manual Sierra, about 33 US mpg, from a 40-liter (10.6-gallon) tank. Bigger tires, roof racks and the 4-speed automatic all make it worse.

Not from the factory: both axles have open differentials, and late trucks add a traction-control mode that only works in low range. BigJimny's owners rate the ARB Air Locker as the best aftermarket option because it's selectable, while Lockright and Kaiser are cheaper automatic lockers that can misbehave on the road.

t: Should I fill the front swivels with oil like a Land Rover?
x: No. BigJimny warns that Land Rover-trained mechanics sometimes try it. The Jimny's knuckle is a greased, 'dry' joint, and its swivel seal acts more as a dust shield and steering damper than an oil seal. Corroded swivel balls aren't critical either: file them smooth and paint them.
Forum regulars advise against them. They shorten the life of the kingpin and wheel bearings dramatically, to as little as six months in hard off-road use according to one experienced owner.

t: Kingpins & Axle Rebuild — BigJimny store (UK), Bits4Vits (UK Suzuki 4x4 parts)
x: The first thing every hard-used Jimny needs. Koyo kingpin bearings, Suzuki seals, preload shims and proper waterproof grease keep the wobble away.

t: Manual Hubs — BigJimny Wiki: manual or fixed hub heads, BigJimny store (UK)
x: Swapping the vacuum hubs for manual or fixed hub heads removes the most failure-prone part of the 4WD system. BigJimny documents every route, from Samurai or Vitara hubs to tailor-made Jimny items.

t: Gearing — BigJimny Wiki: Rock Lobster conversion, Low Range Off-Road
x: The stock low range is tall, and anything over 215/75R15 needs help. The classic fix is a Rock Lobster-style transfer case with lower ratios, or a lower diff ratio from a later VVT truck.
Open diffs front and rear. A selectable air locker in the rear axle is the most popular serious upgrade.

t: Lift & Bushes — BigJimny store (UK), Bits4Vits (UK Suzuki 4x4 parts)
x: Two inches of lift clears 235/75R15s. Caster-correction bushes are fine for a 2-inch lift; BigJimny says a 3-inch lift needs proper replacement arms.

t: Rust Proofing — BigJimny Wiki: rust protection
x: The cheapest mod with the biggest payoff. Clean, seal and wax the underbody and cavities before the rot starts, then touch it up yearly.

M13A: 4.0 L, API SL/SM or newer, 5W-30 or 10W-30 · G13BB: 3.7–4.2 L depending on type Factory filter for the VVT engine is Suzuki 16510-61A31 (16510-61A01 and -61A20 also fit). Replace the sump-plug gasket each time.
Suzuki 13780-81A00 Check it at every oil change on a truck that sees gravel roads.
Not every Jimny has one fitted Purely for the occupants, but worth doing on a dusty import.
M13A VVT: NGK BKR6E-11 / Denso K20PR-U11 (nickel) or NGK IFR6J11 (iridium) Suzuki prefers iridium plugs, especially in cold climates.
M13A VVT: 5.2–5.9 L by type · ethylene glycol, silicate-free From 2005 Suzuki's manuals specify silicate-free coolant, and BigJimny applies that to every gen 3. Flush an unknown truck.
API GL-4 75W-90 · 1.3 L (VVT), 1.1 L (earlier) On an R72 box, a furry drain plug or metal flakes is the early warning of bearing failure.
VVT: Suzuki ATF3317, Mobil ATF3309 or Dexron III · 3.7 L or 5.7 L depending on type BigJimny: the autos 'love fresh ATF'; poor shifts and a top gear that won't select follow neglect.
API GL-4 75W-90 · 1.13 L (VVT), 0.7–0.8 L (earlier) Check the push-button actuator cover for water ingress while you're under there.
API GL-5 80W-90 hypoid · front 1.65 L, rear 1.35 L (VVT); 1.1 L / 1.3 L earlier Milky oil after water crossings means the breathers or seals let water in.
Heavy-duty waterproof grease, not oil BigJimny: the lower bearing can rust solid on trucks that sat for years and show no play at all, so inspect inside on an unknown truck.
PS: Dexron IIE or III · brakes: DOT 3 / SAE J1703 Suzuki doesn't define a power-steering interval; refresh it if it's dark.
G13BB timing belt 12761-70C00 · M13A uses a chain Whirring or squealing on an M13A is usually a drive belt, tensioner or alternator bearing (BigJimny's noise guide).
Exercise 4WD and low range Test hub engagement on a loose surface; dormant vacuum hubs are the usual failure.
Clean to bare metal where rusty, then coat and wax cavities BigJimny: wash the underbody regularly in winter, then drive it dry.

JB64 JB74 JC74 The retro-styled global cult hit with the 1.5 K15B and a 5-door from 2023; not US-importable until 2043. Suzuki styled it like a 1970s LJ, kept the ladder frame and two solid axles, and then watched the whole world queue for it. It's slow, it's tiny and it's illegal to import into America until 2043, which only makes people want one more.

A shaking steering wheel around 45–50 mph, play when a raised front wheel is rocked top to bottom with the brakes held, or oil and grease weeping from the swivel balls. Jack and stands · torque wrench · tie-rod end puller · bearing drift.
Not a fault. The stock suspension rides choppily, sags under accessories and limits tire size. Spring compressor (if needed) · trolley jack and stands · torque wrench · alignment afterward.
A bull bar, winch, roof rack, fridge and two adults put the truck over its factory gross vehicle mass of 1,435–1,450 kg. As for a lift kit · approved installer for certification.

Brake-LSD traction control hesitates or runs out of grip on steep, cross-axled climbs. Unsealed found itself waiting for it to kick in, which cost momentum. Diff setup tools (bearing puller, dial indicator) · compressor and air lines · or a 4x4 shop.

t: Do the first full filter service
x: Unknown service history, a dusty air filter after gravel roads, or a musty cabin. Oil filter wrench · drain pan · basic hand tools.

t: Replace a worn rear wheel bearing
x: A hum or rumble from the rear that changes with speed, or play at the rear wheel when you rock it. Slide hammer or puller · hydraulic press · new retainer ring.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: Stock is 195/80R15. The BigJimny consensus is that 215/75R15 is the biggest that suits the stock rims, though it's only slightly taller. Some Australian owners squeeze 235/75R15s on, but those exceed the stock rims' recommended limits. With a 2-inch lift, 235/75R15s fit with a little trimming of the front bumper. Go bigger and you'll want lower gearing.

t: Can I import a new Jimny into the US?
x: No. It isn't certified for US safety or emissions rules, and NHTSA's exemption only covers vehicles 25 years old from their date of manufacture, which puts the earliest JB74s (built from 29 May 2018) at mid-2043. In 2022 CBP seized a 2022 Jimny bought in Mexico and taken to Puerto Rico, and ordered it brought into compliance, exported or destroyed.

t: What's the difference between the JB64 and JB74?
x: The JB64 is Japan's kei car, with a 658 cc R06A turbo three, no fender flares and a width of 1,475 mm. The JB74 is the 1.5-liter K15B truck with flares and a width of 1,645 mm, sold as the Jimny Sierra in Japan and as the Jimny everywhere else. They share the 2,250 mm wheelbase and the drivetrain layout.

Unsealed 4X4 thinks the long-wheelbase versions of Suzuki 4x4s have always been 'far superior,' with more stability, better climbing and more room. The XL's 2,590 mm wheelbase drops breakover from 27° to 24°, but rear cargo space with the seats up goes from 85 to 211 liters.

Manual, if you can. The automatic is an old four-speed, and Unsealed says the five-speed manual feels like it has an extra 30 kW by comparison. Suzuki Australia rates the manual at 6.4 L/100 km and the auto at 6.9.

t: How much can it tow and carry?
x: Suzuki Australia rates it at 1,300 kg (2,866 lb) braked and 350 kg (772 lb) unbraked, with a 1,450 kg GVM for the 3-door. Unsealed puts real payload at about 340 kg, which a bull bar and winch eat quickly. Towing anything bigger than a small trailer is 'not the droid you're looking for.'

t: Why is it so hard to get one?
x: Demand has run ahead of supply since launch. The UK's 2019 allocation sold out by December 2018, Australia had up to a 12-month queue in 2021, and Japan's 5-door Nomade drew about 50,000 orders in four days in 2025, forcing Suzuki to stop taking orders for a year.

t: Why was it pulled from Europe?
x: CO2. Even the cleanest manual emitted 154 g/km, far above Suzuki's EU fleet target, so the passenger car was withdrawn from the UK in 2020 and replaced by a two-seat commercial version facing a looser 147 g/km target. Wikipedia records that version leaving European sale in 2025.
No. Both diffs are open, and 'brake LSD' traction control brakes a spinning wheel to send torque to the others. ARB lists Air Lockers for the 2019-on Jimny if you want the real thing.

Euro NCAP gave the 2018 3-door Jimny three stars, with 73% for adult occupant protection. Standard equipment varies by market and year. Australian cars now have six airbags, AEB and lane-departure warning, and the 2026 Australian 3-door update added adaptive cruise and front and rear parking sensors.
Japanese tuner DAMD sells 'little G.' body kits for the Jimny Sierra that restyle it as a miniature G-Class.

t: Suspension Lift — Old Man Emu (ARB), Ironman 4x4, EFS
x: 40–50 mm of lift with load-rated springs improves ride, clearance and tire room. Look for kits that include caster correction, brake lines and a panhard bracket.
Legally doubles usable payload for touring in Australia. Ironman's kit takes payload from about 340 kg to 690 kg.
Brake-based traction control is good, but selectable lockers are what turn a Jimny into a rock-hopper.

t: Bar Work & Protection — ARB bull bars, Jimny 2019–present
x: A bull bar for winch mounting and animal strikes, plus underbody protection. Factor the weight into your payload.
Japan's tuning scene loves restyling the Jimny. DAMD's 'little G.' kits for the Jimny Sierra are the best known.
Genuine Gen 4 filters and bearings, plus kingpin parts, shipped from the UK.
